faq_weekPlanReminders_q: Can WitnessWork remind me to plan next week?
faq_weekPlanReminders_a: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Plan Next Week, then choose Remind On and Remind At (Saturday at 6:00 PM unless you change them). At that time, if the following week has no plans yet, you get one reminder inviting you to plan it. Weeks follow your Start of Week setting. Any plan in that week, including a recurring plan, means no reminder, and adding one later clears a reminder you've already received. If you've marked every day as an off day under Availability, you aren't reminded. Tapping the reminder opens the Schedule at that week's month, where you can tap a day to plan it or use the Assistant's suggestions when you have an hour goal. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell until that week ends, even if system notifications are off. It's available for every publisher role. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming, and if you plan on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel the reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_logTimeReminders_q: Can WitnessWork remind me to log time for a day I planned?
faq_logTimeReminders_a: Yes. Go to Preferences → Plans, turn on Remind Me to Log Time, and choose a Remind At time (8:00 PM unless you change it). If a day has a plan but no time logged, you get one reminder at that time after the day's plans end: a morning plan reminds you that evening, and a plan still going at your Remind At time reminds you the next day. Several plans on the same day give one reminder, and when two days' reminders would arrive at the same time they're combined. Logging any time for that day stops its reminder and clears one you've already received; removing that day's plans or turning the setting off does too. A day planned with no time doesn't remind you, and days you missed before turning the setting on aren't included. Tapping the reminder opens Add Time with the date, planned time, and type already filled in. The reminder is also listed in the Home bell for a week, even if system notifications are off. The setting appears when you track hours; Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first. Turning it on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. Reminders are worked out on your device from your own plans and time and aren't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. If you log time on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it can cancel that day's reminder. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_logTimeForDay_q: How do I log time or plan a specific day?
faq_logTimeForDay_a: Tap the day on the Schedule tab, in This Week on Home, or under All Days on the Progress tab. The day opens in the bottom half of the screen, so the calendar or list you tapped stays in view above it, and you can tap another day there to switch to it. If the day has no time logged yet, tap Add Time under Time Reports to unfold the time form right there: tap Time, choose how long, add a note or Type if you like, and tap Submit. If the day has no plans yet, tap Plan Day under Plans the same way: add a title if you like, choose One Time or Recurring and how long, and tap the Add button. Tap Add Time or Plan Day again to fold the form away. To add more time or another plan, tap + beside Time Reports or Plans. Tap an entry to change or delete it, or tap a plan to open it. To log a plan you kept, touch and hold it and choose Log as Time; its length and Type are filled in. These open the form in the same place, and its back arrow returns to the day without saving. A note opens in the note editor over the whole screen; tap Done and the day comes back with the form as you left it. To see more of the day or more of the screen above it, drag the bar at the top of the day up or down; WitnessWork remembers the size on this device. To close the day, tap the X or drag it all the way down; on Android, the back button works too. Logging time appears only if your role logs hours; Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first.
faq_streaks_a: Your streak counts how consistently you keep the plans you make. For pioneers and other roles that log hours, each planned day you log any time on adds one, even if you log less than you planned. Days without a plan don't add to it or end it, so plan the days you mean to go out. For publishers, each month you share in the ministry adds one, whether you mark the month on Home or log time. Your streak shows on Home's header and your Profile once it reaches 3. When logging a day takes it to a milestone, like 3, 5, or 10, a short celebration plays; other days, and growth that arrives another way, such as time logged on your watch or another device, make the flame on Home flare instead. When it's about to end, tap it on Home to log the day that's due. To hide your streak, turn off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges.
faq_streakEnds_q: When does my streak end, and how do I keep it?
faq_streakEnds_a: A planned day can still be logged until the end of the next day. If that passes with no time logged for it, your streak ends. When yours is about to end, the flame on Home shows the time left, and a Streak Reminder comes at 6:00 PM on the last day. For publishers, a month can be recorded until the end of the next month, and the reminder comes three days before that month is over. If you can't go out on a planned day, remove that day's plans ahead of time: tap each one on Schedule, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. For a recurring plan, only that date is removed. The day stays planned while any plan is left on it. If you went out but forgot to log it, add the time on that day and your streak comes back. Turn Streak Reminders off in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges. They need notifications allowed for WitnessWork.
faq_streakBuddies_q: Can my buddies see my streak?
faq_streakBuddies_a: Yes, once it reaches 3, if you share it. Your buddies see the number on your card in their Buddies list, not your time or reports. It's end-to-end encrypted like the rest of what you share. To stop sharing it, open Buddies Settings and turn off Streak. A streak that ended stops showing on your buddies' phones even if your app hasn't opened since.
faq_streaksHide_a: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges and turn off Show streak. Your streak no longer shows on Home or your profile, nothing celebrates it, Streak Reminders stop, and Home's greeting no longer counts days in a row. Your buddies' streaks are hidden too, and yours stops being shared with them. Nothing is lost: your streak comes from your plans and the time you log, so turning Show streak back on shows it again right away, unless it ended in the meantime. The setting follows you to your other devices when sync is on. To hide badges as well, turn off Show badges on the same screen.
faq_navigationShortcuts_q: How do I navigate with keyboard shortcuts on iPad?
faq_navigationShortcuts_a: Connect a hardware keyboard to an iPad running iPadOS 26 or later, then hold Command while the main navigation is visible. Small shortcut labels appear beside the bottom tabs or sidebar items. Press Command and the displayed number to open that screen; release Command to hide the labels. Numbers follow the visible navigation order, so by default Home is Command 1 and Contacts is Command 2. Other numbers depend on which items are visible, including Settings in the sidebar. Close any open form or other screen before using these navigation shortcuts; they do not save or discard records. Only shortcut use is measured, not what you type. Support requires an installed app build with the keyboard feature and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If labels do not appear, check that the keyboard is connected, return to the main navigation, and update and reopen the app. You can always tap navigation items instead. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.

faq_pointerHover_q: How do I use a trackpad, mouse, or Apple Pencil on iPad?
faq_pointerHover_a: Connect a trackpad or mouse to your iPad, or hover a supported Apple Pencil just above the screen. Buttons, rows, and calendar days highlight as the pointer moves over them. When the sidebar is narrowed to icons, resting the pointer on an icon shows its name; other icon-only buttons, such as the map controls and Notifications, also show their names. Hover over the activity grid, the Service Year pace chart, or a mileage bar to see its date and value. On the map, hover a pin to see the contact's name, or hover a contact in the map's side list to name its pin. A secondary click (two-finger click) opens the same menu and preview as touching and holding. The sidebar's resize bar shows arrows for the directions it can still move, and two-finger scrolling moves a contact photo while you crop it. Everything is still available by touch: tap, touch and hold, or drag as usual. Hover changes nothing in your records. Only the fact that a pointer or Pencil was used is measured, at most once a day; no positions, names, or values are sent. On Android, a mouse highlights rows and shows names and chart values, but pins on the map don't show names on hover. iPhone has no hover. If nothing responds, check that the trackpad, mouse, or Pencil is connected, then update and reopen the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep contact details out of public reports.
faq_menuBar_q: How do I use the menu bar on iPad?
faq_menuBar_a: On iPadOS 26 or later, use Windowed Apps or Stage Manager and swipe down from the top edge to reveal the menu bar. After setup, WitnessWork Preferences opens in-app settings; the standard Settings item opens your device's settings. File opens Log Visit…, Add Time when hours logging is enabled, Add Contact, New Plan, and Backup & Restore. Edit → Find Contact opens the Contacts list and focuses search. Help opens the Help Center, What's New, your email app for private support, or Check for Update. These shortcuts reuse the existing screens; opening a form does not save or share your records. Check for Update checks for a compatible app update and uses the existing download and restart flow when one is available. It cannot install a new native app version, and is unavailable in development builds. Menu-bar support requires an installed app build that includes it and is unavailable on iPhone and Android. If items are missing, update from your app store and reopen WitnessWork. You can still use the same actions inside the app. For other problems, use the Help Center's private email link and keep contact details and backups out of public reports.
faq_appLock_q: How do I lock WitnessWork with Face ID or Touch ID?
faq_appLock_a: Open Settings → Security and turn on Require Face ID (Require Touch ID or Require Passcode on devices without Face ID; Require Biometric Unlock on Android). WitnessWork asks you to confirm it's you before it turns on. From then on, WitnessWork asks you to unlock it every time it opens. Use Require to choose whether it asks again as soon as you leave the app, or only after 1, 5, or 15 minutes away. If Face ID, Touch ID, or your fingerprint isn't recognized, use your device passcode, PIN, pattern, or password instead. The lock is on this device only: it isn't synced, saved in backups, or sent anywhere, so turn it on separately on each device. Your device needs a passcode, or on Android a screen lock (PIN, pattern, or password); if your Android device has none, tap Open Settings when WitnessWork asks, set one up, then turn the lock on again. If you remove it later, WitnessWork opens without asking. While the lock is on, the app switcher (Recents on Android) shows a blank card instead of WitnessWork's screen; on Android, this needs Android 13 or later. The lock covers the app itself; widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri, and your watch still show what they normally do. To turn it off, open Settings → Security, turn the switch off, and confirm it's you. If unlocking keeps failing, check that your device passcode works on the lock screen, then force-quit and reopen WitnessWork. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep personal details out of public reports.

1110.c2: Adjusted various styles to better fit larger screens.
1110.c3: Adjusted the method of submitting Bug Reports and Feature Requests to Github.

1111.c1: Add donate page in the settings for those who wish to contribute.
1111.c2: Includes various minor improvements and bug fixes

1200.c1: Adds backup and restore functionality. Now you can backup your data to the cloud and restore it later, this allows you to transfer your data to another device. You can also transfer it to another platform. Find this new feature in settings.

1201.c1: Updates monthly routine section of home screen to show surrounding months.
1201.c2: Significantly improved Korean translations - thank you brother Paul. If you'd like to help translate your own language, please visit the settings.

1210.c1: Greatly improved accuracy of time displays.
1210.c2: Improved accuracy of time progress bars.
1210.c3: Added helpful hints for actions that may not be immediately noticeable.
1210.c4: Improved quality of life on the maps screen with more relevant information and a quick-add button.

1211.c1: Added more helpful one-time hints when appropriate.

1220.c3: Added Calendar to time reports screen.
1220.c1: Preferences are now better organized by category.
1220.c2: Improved import & export screen to be visually clearer.
1220.c4: Occasionally notifies you to create a new backup. This is configurable in the settings.

1221.c1: [iOS] Date and Time pickers now use the correct locale
1221.c2: Fixed an issue where editing a conversation would incorrectly navigate.
1221.c3: Other minor bug fixes and performance improvements.
1221.c4: Improved Spanish translation - thank you brother Cleen. If you'd like to help translate your own language, see 'Help Translate' in the settings.

1230.c1: Added new Annual Overview screen to view your service year progress by month.
1230.c2: Added 'Today' button to quickly navigate back to current month when viewing previous months or years.
1230.c3: Updated Special Pioneers to not have an annual goal by default.
1230.c4: Added 'Annual Goal' setting to publisher preferences. This allows you to override the default setting for your publisher type.
1230.c5: Greatly improved Italian translations, thank you brother Giuseppe!

1240.c1: Added ability to manually adjust contact pin location on all map views. Simply touch, hold, and drag the pin.
1240.c2: Added small map view to contact details screen and resolved errors for invalid coordinates.
1240.c3: Resolved an overflow visual issue that sometimes occurs on small screens when viewing map contact cards.

1250.c1: Big update! Added scheduling & plans! 🚀 You can now create one-time plans, recurring plans, and view your month's schedule.
1250.c2: Improved clarity by adding 'toast' notifications for notable app actions.
1250.c3: Updated various sections of time reports screen to have more information and easier navigation.
1250.c4: Resolved minor visual issues and other bugs.
1250.c5: Added font size offset setting to preferences. This allows you to adjust the font size of the app.

1260.c1: Fixed issue where scroll position would be lost on TimeReportsScreen. Resolved other issues related to time reports screen.
1260.c2: LDC hours do not contribute more towards annual goal past 55 hours for any given month.
1260.c3: Recurring plans can be deleted by single event or single event and all future events.
1260.c4: New custom fields for contacts! You can create any number of custom fields you wish.
1260.c5: You can now share your time directly with NW Publisher!

1270.c1: Added Timer! ⏱️ (Stopwatch). You can now start and stop a timer to track your time directly within the app.
1270.c2: Resolved crashing issue for some devices when navigating to the Contact Details screen.
1270.c4: Other minor bug fixes and improvements.

1280.c3: Update dependencies and add security updates.
1280.c2: Updated Portuguese translations, thank you brother Sérgio!
1280.c4: 📝 A little personal note: I have been very busy with congregation responsibilities and life recently. After my upcoming convention next week, things will return more back to normal. I will be working on many more updates in the coming weeks! Thank you for your patience and for choosing WitnessWork! ❤️

1290.c1: Added new schedule section to month summary screen which helps you keep track of your time pacing.
1290.c2: On home screen, resolved overlapping issues that sometimes happen on small screen sizes.
1290.c3: You can now edit time entries! Tap on them!
1290.c4: Many improvements have been made to clarity of how to add, update, and delete various items across WitnessWork. Hints have been removed as they're no longer necessary.
1290.c5: I'm looking for 2 volunteers who have experience in Software QA to assist in testing releases before they reach the public. If you have interest in spending a few hours a month testing, your support would be greatly appreciated. Please contact me: levi@leviwilkerson.com. In the future and as expenses allows, a portion of donations will go to QA for their time.
1290.c6: Annual time overview screen now is compressed for better readability.

1291.c1: [ANDROID] Resolved crashes that occurred when editing time.

1300.c1: Add 'Annual Schedule' to Plan Schedule screen for those with an annual goal, allowing you to easily see if you have planned enough time for your entire service year.
1300.c2: Hides 'today' schedule view when the month is in the future because it's not applicable.
1300.c4: If a contact pin was dragged for a contact, navigation will now prioritize the manually adjusted pin over their address. Editing a contact's address will return the address to priority.
1300.c7: Contact pin colors on Contact Details Screen now matches the map screen.
1300.c9: Month and annual total calculations now properly limit your credit time to 55 hours per month. Standard time is not affected by this rule. If you exceed this time using credit, you'll have overage displayed on your month's details screen.
1300.c10: Added time credit support. Existing users will be able to update their old time entries automatically.
1300.c11: Resolved issue with add button overlapping compass on iOS.

1310.c1: Greatly improved performance when navigating to time related screens.
1310.c3: Resolve date localization issue that occurred in some regions.
1310.c4: Updated styles and locations of commonly used items. Month and Service Year reports can be easily accessed in the tab bar at the bottom of the screen.
1310.c5: Resolved style overflow issues that occurred on certain screen sizes for the map screen.
1310.c6: Now automatically prefills recently used addresses when creating multiple contacts on the same day.
1310.c7: You can now toggle visibility of the home screen sections. Visit Preferences > Home Screen.
1310.c8: The app now is named WitnessWork, formerly 'JW Time' due to legal reasons.
1310.c9: Languages now attempt to find your exact region, otherwise it falls back to any locale with your language. If nothing can be found, it defaults to English.
1310.c10: Bemba language added! We need your help to translate. Please visit Settings > Help Translate

1320.c1: Now create coordinate only contacts. If your territory is very rural or with bad mapping information, there is now no need to rely on an address.
1320.c2: Easily toggle between device, dark, and light mode color scheme. Visit Preferences > Appearance.
1320.c4: 'Add Time' screen now allows for increments of 1 minute.
1320.c5: Added Kinyarwanda language, fully translated by Semana D. Thank you so much for your help!
1320.c6: You can now select how your time is displayed. Choose between decimal like: 13.5 or choose 13 Hrs 30 Mins. Visit Preferences > Appearance.

1330.c1: Added language selector. See Preferences to manually adjust your language.
1330.c2: Resolved issue with one-time plan having an inaccurate maximum date.

1340.c1: Added a special reward for when you check off your time box or add time!
1340.c2: You can now set a decimal value for hour goals on 'custom' publisher type.

1350.c1: You can now use autocomplete to search for an address! Just start typing to see suggestions. This feature is only possible by your generous donations. Thank you for your support!
1350.c2: Resolved issue where day sheet would not close automatically when adding time to a day of month.
1350.c3: Resolved overflow issue on home screen for tablets.

1360.c1: New: Share Contacts and easily import them. Transferring calls is now easier than ever.
1360.c2: You can now customize the colors of the pins on the map.
1360.c3: New: Dismiss Contact feature. You can now dismiss contacts you no longer wish to visit and receive notifications when it's time to return to them.
1360.c4: Added notes support to time reports.
1360.c5: Enhanced recurring plan scheduling - You can now schedule plans monthly by day of week (e.g., 'first Monday of every month').
1360.c7: Added statistics sections to your Monthly and Yearly reports to better track your progress and patterns.
1360.c8: You can now change your calendar's first day of the week. Visit Preferences > Appearance.
1360.c10: Follow up topic now supports multiple lines.
1360.c11: There are now no restrictions on when you can add time or schedule plans.
1360.c12: Added visual indicators on calendar days to show when notes are present.
1360.c13: Resolves issue with Korean and Panama phone number formatting.
1360.c14: Contact Details Screen map is now zoomed out to easily see surroundings at a glance.
1360.c15: Fixed various navigation issues when adding time and scheduling plans.
1360.c16: Improved readability and consistency throughout the app with better spacing and button sizes.

1382.c1: The Milestone Update is here. A whole new look with a floating tab bar, frosted cards, and a fresh, modern feel throughout the app.
1382.c2: New Contacts tab with fuzzy search, smart sort, and stacked filters. Your contacts are now a first-class destination.
1382.c3: Progress Screen 2.0: a fresh look at Month, Year, and All-time, with customizable milestones, category breakdowns, and lifetime hours.
1382.c4: iCloud sync arrives (Supporter): your reports, contacts, and plans stay in step across all your devices. Optional photo sync keeps avatars synced too.
1382.c5: Onboarding has been rebuilt from the ground up. A personal note from the developer, animated plan previews, and a checklist tailored to your goals.
1382.c6: Brand new home screen widgets: month calendar, appointments, hours, and contacts. All one tap away.
1382.c7: Contact avatars are here. Photos or emoji, with a tap-to-expand fullscreen viewer.
1382.c8: Share a contact with another publisher via secure universal links.
1382.c9: Smarter recurring plans. Schedule by day-of-week and week-of-month, with per-instance overrides and deletions.
1382.c10: Time rollover: fractional minutes carry forward into the next month, manually or automatically.
1382.c11: Beautiful new celebrations the moment you cross a goal.
1382.c12: New Supporter tier with personalization, including a custom accent color.
1382.c13: Schedule screen: a focused calendar view of day plans and recurring conversations.
1382.c14: A redesigned profile card on the home screen showing your role, time served, and fun stats.
1382.c15: Approaching and missed conversations now surface on the home screen so you never lose track.
1382.c16: Phone region code now persists across new contacts. Phone region search is faster and more accurate.
1382.c17: Map empty state, location prompts, and contact map clustering have all been polished.
1382.c18: Countless small bug fixes, performance improvements, and visual refinements throughout the app.

1383.c1: Plans now have a Type. Assign a category to a scheduled plan and your projected totals reflect the right kind of credit.
1383.c2: Projected totals are more accurate. They respect your monthly credit cap and no longer double-count time you've already logged today.
1383.c3: The celebration chime once again respects your ring/silent switch.
1383.c5: New contacts and address edits now save immediately, even before the geocode api finishes locating them.
1383.c6: The calendar refreshes right away after you add, edit, or remove a plan.
1383.c7: Map pins stay in focus after you tap them. Resolve intermittent issue with map refocusing incorrect contact pin.
1383.c8: Smoother scrolling in the Contacts list. Resolve issues with contacts disappearing.
1383.c4: Your Donations now shows the correct billing period and price for annual and granted supporter subscriptions.

1400.c1: Switching from MyTime? You can now import your contacts and visit history straight from a MyTime backup, with a preview before anything is added, so there's no manual re-entry.
1400.c2: Date format, clock style, and start of the week are now separate from your app language. Set each one in Settings > Date & Time, with an Auto option that follows your region or device.
1400.c3: You can now customize the day thresholds and colors behind contact staleness. Tune them in Settings > Personalization > Color Key.
1400.c4: Resolved an issue with the map search auto closing.
1400.c5: Locating contacts on the map now shows live progress, and you can skip it midway without losing your place.
1400.c6: Faster, smoother scrolling in the Contacts list, plus quicker home screen widget updates.
1400.c7: Fixed projected totals around time zone changes, enlarged header buttons for easier tapping, and polished countless small details throughout the app.

1411.c1: New: Meet Scribe AI. Paste your field-ministry notes, whether a handwritten-style log or an export from another app, and Scribe AI turns them into contacts, visits, and time entries for you to review before anything is saved. Refine the results by chatting inline, start an import right from onboarding, and never lose a credit on an import that finds nothing.
1411.c2: A new customizable This Month dashboard on the home screen. Your goal, projection, and schedule pace live in cards you can arrange and expand, while your Service Report stays in one clean card. Tap the report for a full breakdown.
1411.c3: Monthly goal overrides. Set a different goal for a single month when your circumstances change, and see your planned hours as their own progress ring.
1411.c4: Plan more than one thing per day. Day plans on the same date now add together, each keeping its own category, and plans that do not count toward a day are clearly marked.
1411.c5: Easier editing everywhere. Plans, time entries, and conversations now have an ellipsis menu for Edit and Delete, and recurring plans offer clear choices for changing one date, future dates, or the whole series.
1411.c6: Service Reports: Hourglass and NW Publisher submission are back, you can pick a default submission method, edit the report comment before sending, and get a month-end reminder. The year-by-year history can now be trimmed or backfilled with earlier years.
1411.c7: Schedule now shows each day's status at a glance: ahead, behind, on track, upcoming, matched, or no plan.
1411.c8: Supporter status now follows your Apple ID across devices, Scribe AI allowances roll over on a schedule, and the Supporter screen has been simplified.
1411.c9: Fixed time entries and plans landing on the wrong day in time zones at UTC+12 and beyond, plus wrong-day dates late in the evening west of UTC. Fixed map pins opening the wrong contact after swiping the card carousel. Time rollover now keeps Credit Time in its original month by default.
1411.c10: The Credit toggle on categories is now available to every hours-based role. Also fixed a rare crash when closing a picker, restored favorite stars and the current-month Bible study icon, updated to Expo SDK 57, and trimmed the app size.

1420.c1: New iPad layouts show contacts, maps, and schedules alongside their details.
1420.c2: Customize contact fields: reorder phone, email, and custom fields, hide phone or email, and permanently delete archived custom fields.
1420.c3: See your logged time by category across the Service Year, and adjust the monthly credit limit in supported Publisher preferences.
1420.c4: Hourglass submissions now separate preaching time from Credit Time.
1420.c5: The calendar Assistant is available again, with controls in Schedule preferences.

1430.c1: Data protection mode for publishers in the EU, the UK and Switzerland keeps householder records to what the law allows, including consent tracking and cleanup of contacts you haven't visited in a while.
1430.c2: Create a contact right from a pin you drop on the map.
1430.c3: Kingdom Publishers can choose to log their hours with a timer, an optional monthly goal and the Progress tab.
1430.c4: The Year tab now shows your service-year total for every role, even without an annual goal.
1430.c5: Follow-ups on visits are now optional, and you can turn off app sounds in Preferences.
1430.c6: Fixed dates shifting for publishers in far-east time zones.

1440.c1: Simpler navigation with four labeled tabs you can reorder. The map now lives at the top of Contacts, and Settings is under your profile picture.
1440.c2: Contacts are redesigned around what's next, with every visit on a timeline. Log a visit from the + menu with nearby suggestions, and add custom fields to conversations.
1440.c3: Schedule has a zoomable year and month calendar, and a plan can be just hours or a time span.
1440.c4: See your service year's pace month by month, and celebrate streaks and badges along the way.
1440.c5: Optional mileage tracking logs your trips and fuel costs.
1440.c6: Follow-ups can sync to a calendar just for WitnessWork, now on Android too, where you can also back up and sync with Google Drive.
1440.c7: Reminders wait in the notification bell instead of piling up on Home.

buddies_syncUnverified: Can't verify this device, so Buddies isn't available.
buddies_syncVerifyLater: Couldn't verify this device yet. Showing saved buddies.
buddies_invitesFooter: Each invite works once and expires after 7 days.
buddies_enterInviteLink_description: Paste the link your buddy sent you.
buddies_invalidLink: That isn't a Buddies invite link.
buddies_pasteInviteLinkHintAndroid: Copy the invite link your buddy sent you, then tap Enter Invite Link again.
buddies_cancelInviteBody: The link and QR code will stop working.
buddies_inviteA11y: Invite a buddy with a link
buddies_codeHint: Have your buddy scan this Buddies Code in WitnessWork. It works once.
buddies_codeFull: All {{max}} spots are in use. Remove a buddy or cancel an invite to add someone new.
buddies_codeError: We couldn't create a code. Check your connection and try again.
buddies_scanHint: Point your camera at your buddy's Buddies Code.

buddies_planTimesInfo: Buddies see which days you plan to go out and for how long. Time of day shows Morning, Afternoon, or Evening in place of the start time.
buddies_pauseSharingInfo: Buddies stop seeing your plans, streak, badges, and pet until the pause ends. They still see your name and photo, and they aren't told. Invitations you send still go out.
buddies_pauseIndefinitely: Until I turn it back on
buddies_shareMyPlansInfo: Buddies see which days you go out and for how long. Turned off, they see none of your plans, and aren't told.
buddies_showOnCalendarInfo: Shows the days buddies plan to go out on your calendar. Plans you go out on together always show.
buddies_scopeAllEveryone: These apply to every buddy. Choose a buddy above to change something just for them.

buddies_scopeAllSomeOwn.one: These apply to every buddy. 1 buddy has settings of their own.
buddies_scopeAllSomeOwn.other: These apply to every buddy. {{count}} buddies have settings of their own.

buddies_scopeBuddyFollows: {{name}} follows All Buddies. Change anything here to make it just for them.
buddies_settingsResetAllLabel: Have {{name}} follow All Buddies in everything
buddies_onboardingWelcomeBody: Pair with up to 5 friends you go out in service with, and see each other's planned days right on your calendar.
buddies_onboardingEncryptedBody: Everything you share is encrypted on your phone. Only you and the buddies you choose can read it — not even WitnessWork can.
buddies_onboardingControlBody: Nothing is shared until you both agree. Hide a buddy from your calendar or remove them anytime — they won't be notified.
buddies_accountNameHint: Buddies see you as %{name}, the name on your account. Change your name here to change it for them.
buddies_onboardingProfileInfo: Buddies see your name and the days you plan to go out over the next 8 weeks, with how long you plan. Your photo, pioneer status, streak, badges, pet, and start times are shared unless you turn them off. Change any of it, or pause sharing, in Buddies Settings. Your recorded hours, reports, goals, contacts, visits, and notes always stay private. Plan and Follow-up invitations share the extra details shown in the form.
buddies_inviteShareMessage: Let's plan our ministry together with WitnessWork Buddies. Tap this link to be buddies — it works once and expires in 7 days: {{link}}
buddies_limitReached: You can have up to {{max}} buddies, including pending invites.
buddies_openInvitesLimit: You have {{max}} invites waiting to be accepted. Cancel one to make another.
buddies_nameRequired: Add your name to your profile first so your buddy knows who you are.
buddies_requestBody: Confirm only if you invited {{name}}. Nothing is shared until you do.
buddies_removePending: Removed from this device, but we couldn't reach the server to finish. Your buddy may still see your plans until you're back online — we'll keep trying.
buddies_removeBody: {{name}} won't be notified, but may notice. You'll both stop seeing each other right away, and reconnecting takes a new invite.
buddies_notificationsOff: Turn on notifications to hear when a buddy accepts, confirms, invites you, or replies.
buddies_notificationsInfo: When someone accepts your invite or confirms your request, and when a buddy invites you to something, changes or cancels it, or replies.
buddies_deleteAllBody: You'll be removed from every buddy's app, and your pending invites will stop working. Your encrypted Buddies data is erased from our server and from all your devices, and your recovery key changes. Your buddies won't be notified. This can't be undone.
buddies_deleteAllBodyBackup: You'll be removed from every buddy's app, and your pending invites will stop working. Your encrypted Buddies data is erased from our server and from all your devices, your WitnessWork backup is deleted, and your recovery key changes. Your buddies won't be notified. This can't be undone.
buddies_deleteAllBackupFailed: Your WitnessWork backup couldn't be deleted first, so nothing changed. Check your connection, then try again.
buddies_deletedNewKeyBody: Your backup continues under your new account. Save your new recovery key from Settings → Account → Show Recovery Key.
buddies_deleteAllPending: We couldn't finish deleting your Buddies data. Your buddies may still see your plans until it's done. Try again when you're connected.

buddies_invitePlansHorizon: Planned days and times, 8 weeks ahead
buddies_invitePrivate: Hours, reports, and notes stay private

buddies_pushPairConfirmedBody: You can now see each other's planned service days.

buddies_pushPlanCancelBody: A buddy canceled a Plan you were invited to.

notesImport_privacySummary: Scribe AI sends your notes through OpenRouter to trusted Western language-model providers with Zero Data Retention, so they aren't stored. Notes are held only while the import runs; your history stays on your device. WitnessWork never sells or shares your notes or uses them to train models. Voice logs and scanned pages are turned into text on your device, and the audio and scans are never uploaded. Photos you choose are read the same way as your notes, through Zero Data Retention providers, and aren't stored.

faq_notesFormatting_q: How do I format a note?
faq_notesFormatting_a: Tap the note in a visit, time entry, plan, or trip to open the note editor. The bar above the keyboard adds headings, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, bulleted and numbered lists, checklists, and links. Swipe the bar sideways to see every button; the button at its right end puts the keyboard away. Your note is kept with the visit, entry, plan, or trip when you tap Save or Add. Links show a preview card under the note, and you can tick off checklist items right where the note is shown. Service report comments and follow-up topics stay plain text.
faq_notesPhotos_q: How do I add photos to a note?
faq_notesPhotos_a: In the note editor, tap the photo button, then Take Photo or Choose Photos. A note holds up to 10 photos. To make one smaller or bigger, tap it while editing and drag a corner; it keeps that share of the note's width on every device. Photos are resized and saved on this device; tap one in a note to see it full screen or share it. With data protection mode on, visit notes can't hold photos, because a photo of someone's home is personal information about them. Photos reach your other devices only when Include photos is on in iCloud Sync (Google Drive Sync on Android); Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet. Backup files and contact shares leave them out. A Plan you invite buddies to shares its note's photos too, end-to-end encrypted; a buddy sees a placeholder until a photo finishes downloading, or while photo sharing is paused. Shared photos are deleted from WitnessWork's servers a month after the Plan, or right away when you remove them, delete the Plan, or stop sharing it.
faq_notesSync_q: Why is a photo missing from a note, or a note plain on another device?
faq_notesSync_a: A note says “This photo isn't on this device” when the photo hasn't reached this device: photo sync is off here or on the device that added it, or the photo is still uploading. Turn on Include photos in iCloud Sync (Google Drive Sync on Android) on both devices and open the app on the device that added the photo; the photo appears after the next sync. Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet, so on Cloud Sync a photo stays on the device that added it. Restoring a backup file doesn't bring photos back. A device with an older version of WitnessWork shows notes as plain text, without formatting or photos, and editing a note there replaces its formatting everywhere. Update WitnessWork on every device to keep it.
faq_timeRollover_q: Does my time automatically roll over to the next month?
faq_timeRollover_a: Yes. Partial hours below your monthly goal can carry over to the next month. Open Settings → Profile → Advanced and turn on Automatic time rollover (shown when you log hours). The carried hours appear automatically when the new month begins, so you don't need to manually subtract or re-enter anything.
faq_bibleStudies_a: Studies are tracked per contact, not per day. To count a study, open a contact, log a conversation, and mark it as "Conducted Bible Study." That contact will count as 1 study for the current month, even if you have multiple sessions with them. To raise your study count, mark a study conversation with a different contact. Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so they don't count; once you log your own study with that contact, it counts.
faq_iCloudSync_q: Can I sync my data between devices?
faq_iCloudSync_a: iCloud Sync is a Supporter feature on iOS. Open Settings → Sync on each supported device, choose iCloud, and use the same iCloud account to sync your service records, contacts, visits, and preferences. Photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. Without an internet connection, the status says Waiting for connection; your changes are saved on the device and sync when you're back online. If a device signs in to a different Apple Account, iCloud Sync turns off there before any records are read or sent, and they stay on the device; turn sync back on to choose how to combine it with that account’s iCloud data. That device also stops sharing Supporter status from your previous account; if it was bought with this device’s App Store account, use Restore Purchases. A device set up from another device’s backup syncs as its own device automatically. Calendar Sync is a separate, free feature that publishes your upcoming Follow-ups to a dedicated calendar; it does not sync your app records between devices. Cloud Sync, the other option in Settings → Sync, is end-to-end encrypted and also syncs between an iPhone and an Android phone (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). A device syncs with one option at a time, and only with your devices on the same option, so choose the same one on each. On Android, Supporters can also sync between Android phones and tablets with Google Drive Sync (see “How do I sync my data between Android devices?”). To move to a new phone, including from an iPhone to an Android phone, see “How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?”.
faq_googleDriveSync_q: How do I sync my data between Android devices?
faq_googleDriveSync_a: Google Drive Sync is a Supporter feature on Android, in beta. On each Android phone or tablet, open Settings → Sync, choose Google Drive, and turn on Sync with Google Drive, then choose the same Google Account in Google's window and allow WitnessWork to keep its data in your Google Drive. It syncs your service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, mileage, profile, and shared preferences; photos have a separate Include images in sync switch. Each device has its own switch, and settings like data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding stay on each device. While WitnessWork is open, changes from your other devices arrive within about a minute, and otherwise the next time you open it; tap Sync now to check right away. On a new Android device, choose From Google Drive on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen to restore your data, which also brings your Supporter status over once that Google Account is connected. If a device connects a different Google Account, sync turns off there before anything is read or sent, and your records stay on the device. Google Drive Sync syncs only with your other Android devices that use it. To sync between an iPhone and an Android device, use Cloud Sync in Settings → Sync instead (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). To move your records to another phone, use Cloud Sync, Backup in Settings → Account, or a backup file from Settings → Backup & Restore.
faq_googleDriveSyncPrivacy_q: What does Google Drive Sync store, and who can see it?
faq_googleDriveSyncPrivacy_a: Each Android device keeps one copy of your WitnessWork data, plus optional photos, in a hidden app folder in the Google Drive of the account you connected. Only WitnessWork can open that folder: it doesn't appear in the Drive app or website, other apps can't read it, and WitnessWork can't see anything else in your Drive. Your data goes straight between your device and Google and never passes through WitnessWork's servers. Google stores it under your Google Account like your other Drive files; it isn't end-to-end encrypted. WitnessWork keeps only a one-way code for the connected account on the device, not your email. The folder counts against your Google storage. To remove it, turn off sync on every device, then in Google Drive on the web open Settings → Manage apps → WitnessWork → Options → Delete hidden app data. Disconnecting Google Drive in Settings → Google Drive Sync stops access from that device and leaves the folder for your other devices. To remove WitnessWork's access for every device, remove it under Third-party apps & services in your Google Account. Your JSON backups from Settings → Backup & Restore are separate and stay wherever you save them.
faq_googleDriveSyncTroubleshooting_q: Google Drive Sync isn't working on my Android device. What can I check?
faq_googleDriveSyncTroubleshooting_a: Open Settings → Sync and read the status. Check that every device uses Google Drive and is connected to the same Google Account and that Google Play services is installed and up to date. If the status says to reconnect, tap Reconnect Google Drive and allow access again; Google asks again if access was removed in your Google Account settings. If your Google storage is full, your changes stay on this device until there's room; free up space or get more storage, then tap Sync now. Sync needs an internet connection; the status says Waiting for connection until you're back online, and changes made offline are sent then while WitnessWork is open. If it says Google Drive is busy, Google is limiting requests for a while; your changes stay on this device and sync tries again on its own. If a device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update every device. Google Drive Sync requires Supporter access; if it lapses, sync pauses and resumes when access returns. Keep an exported backup and the device with your latest data before rebuilding Google Drive data. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing still fails, and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_calendarSetup_q: How do I show Follow-ups in my calendar?
faq_calendarSetup_a: Calendar Sync is free on iPhone, iPad, and Android. This answer covers iPhone and iPad, and How does Calendar Sync work on Android? covers Android. During first-time setup, or from the invitation in the notifications tray after updating, tap Add to Calendar to create a WitnessWork calendar (in iCloud when available). You can also set it up anytime in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync: allow full calendar access, then create a WitnessWork calendar or choose a calendar used only for WitnessWork. Updates need iCloud sign-in and an internet connection, even for Google or Outlook calendars. To use Google or Outlook, create a calendar with that provider, add the account in iPhone Settings → Apps → Calendar → Calendar Accounts, and turn on its calendars. Your default calendar and calendars stored only on this device can't be selected. Once a calendar is selected, every upcoming Follow-up is added automatically, including ones you already saved, as a 30-minute event. Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none; to stop adding them, turn it off in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync. Past Follow-ups, service Plans, and recurring Plans aren't added. Each event gets the same alert as its Follow-up's Notify Me reminder, and no alert when Notify Me is off. Your calendar provider may add its own default alerts; for Google, remove them under that calendar's Event notifications in Google Calendar settings. Make changes in WitnessWork, because calendar edits, including alerts, may be replaced on the next update.
faq_calendarPrivacy_q: What does Calendar Sync share or store?
faq_calendarPrivacy_a: By default, published events contain a generic Follow-up title, the appointment time and duration, and a link that opens the Visit in WitnessWork. Include names and addresses is optional and applies across your devices; turning it on adds those details to published events. Visit notes and Follow-up topics are never exported. Your chosen calendar provider may sync events to other devices, shared calendars, and widgets, so check that calendar's sharing settings before including details. WitnessWork manages only events it marked as its own and does not import your personal calendar appointments. A private iCloud record stores device names and opaque identifiers, publishing ownership, the connected calendar's name and account label, shared options, and event identifiers. Appointment content stays in the chosen calendar account. Each device's calendar identifier and connection state stay local and are separate from app-data sync and backup files.
faq_calendarPrimary_q: Why does Calendar Sync use a primary device?
faq_calendarPrimary_a: Exactly one device publishes your Follow-ups to avoid competing updates. The first device to connect becomes primary. On iOS devices using the same iCloud account, open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync to register each device, view the Primary device list, and choose a primary. Calendar Sync itself does not require Supporter. Follow-ups edited on another device reach the primary through existing app-data sync, which still requires Supporter and sync turned on in Settings → Sync; open WitnessWork on the primary to publish them. After a transfer, the new primary needs access to the same calendar account and full calendar permission. If a transfer is pending, reopen WitnessWork on the previous primary so it can finish its interrupted operation. There is no automatic timeout takeover if that device is permanently unavailable; use private support under Still need help? in the Help Center. Removing a stale device from the list does not delete its app records or calendar events.
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_q: Calendar events are missing or updates are paused. What should I do?
faq_calendarTroubleshooting_a: If Calendar Sync stops updating, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray (the bell on Home): right away when something needs you, such as calendar access, or after a day for problems that often clear on their own, like no internet connection. Tap it for the fix, or choose Turn Off if you no longer want Follow-ups in your calendar. You can also open Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync and read the displayed error. If WitnessWork needs calendar access, tap Open iPhone Settings, tap Calendars, and choose Full Access; Add Events Only isn't enough. When you come back to WitnessWork, setup or updates continue on their own. For connection problems, check your internet connection, iCloud sign-in, and calendar account, then tap Try Again. If setup says no calendar account can hold a WitnessWork calendar, turn on iCloud Calendars in iPhone Settings, then tap Try Again. Use Sync now on the primary device after your calendar account and app data finish syncing. A missing calendar must be reconnected or replaced; calendars renamed outside WitnessWork may need to be chosen again. When a previously published future event is missing, updates pause even if this device published it: calendar sync delays, deletion, and moving an event can look the same. Wait for the calendar account to finish syncing and confirm you chose the same dedicated calendar. Move any WitnessWork events you moved elsewhere back before retrying. Restore missing events is an explicit recovery option after those checks; it can create duplicates if copies are still downloading or remain elsewhere. A past Follow-up is not initially added. For pending device transfers, reopen the previous primary. If the problem continues, use the Help Center's private support option and include the app version, device and operating-system version, and the error shown. Keep contact details, calendar screenshots, notes, and backups out of public reports.
faq_calendarDisconnect_q: What happens when I turn off Calendar Sync or uninstall WitnessWork?
faq_calendarDisconnect_a: In Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, choose Turn Off Calendar Sync, or choose Turn Off on a Calendar updates paused notification. On the primary device, the one that updates your calendar, you can keep the events already added or remove them. Remove Events removes the marked events from the selected calendar, including previously exported history; unrelated events and the calendar itself remain. Turning it off on the primary stops updates from every device. On any other device, Calendar Sync turns off on that device only and the events stay. Events you keep, or that are left after uninstalling, are no longer updated until you set Calendar Sync up again. Uninstalling WitnessWork does not remove calendar events. You can remove an unused dedicated calendar in your calendar app after checking that it contains nothing you want to keep. Turning off Calendar Sync does not delete your Contacts, Visits, or Follow-ups in WitnessWork.
faq_calendarAndroid_q: How does Calendar Sync work on Android?
faq_calendarAndroid_a: Calendar Sync is free on Android. During first-time setup, from the invitation in the notifications tray, or in Settings → Preferences → Calendar Sync, tap Add to Calendar or Choose a calendar, then allow calendar access. Create a WitnessWork calendar on this device, or choose an existing calendar used only for WitnessWork, such as one you created in Google Calendar and set to sync to this phone. A calendar created on the device stays on this device; a Google calendar also shows on your other devices and on the web. Main calendars can't be selected. Every upcoming Follow-up is then added as a 30-minute event with the same alert as its Notify Me reminder; Calendar Sync adds all of your upcoming Follow-ups or none. Past Follow-ups and Plans aren't added. Updates run when you open WitnessWork and after you save changes, and Sync now updates right away. Each event's description holds a WitnessWork link that identifies its Follow-up, so an update changes the existing event instead of adding another, even when another Android device updates the same Google calendar. Don't edit that link. An event you delete in your calendar app comes back on the next update. Android has no primary device and doesn't use iCloud, and Include names and addresses applies to this device only. If updates stop, for example because calendar access was turned off, a Calendar updates paused notification appears in the notifications tray; tap it for the fix, or open Calendar Sync to read the error. For calendar access, tap Open Settings, then Permissions → Calendar → Allow; setup or updates continue when you come back to WitnessWork. For other errors, tap Try Again. Turn Off Calendar Sync keeps or removes WitnessWork events; it never deletes the calendar or your other events. Uninstalling WitnessWork leaves its events, so remove them first if you don't want them. If the problem continues, use the private support option under Still need help? in the Help Center, and keep contact details and calendar screenshots out of public reports.
faq_widgets_q: Are there home or lock screen widgets?
faq_widgets_a: Yes, on iOS. Long-press your home or lock screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and pick the widget you want. Service Report shows this month's hours toward your goal and how much a day it takes to reach it, on your home or lock screen; if you don't log hours, it shows this month's conversations and studies, counted as in the app. Calendar, Appointments, Contacts, and Pet Companion go on your home screen. Widgets move on to the new day at midnight even if you don't open WitnessWork; if one looks out of date, open the app.
faq_appleWatch_q: Is there an Apple Watch app?
faq_appleWatch_a: Yes, for iPhone with an Apple Watch on watchOS 26 or later. It installs automatically if Automatic App Install is on; otherwise open the Watch app on your iPhone, find WitnessWork under Available Apps, and tap Install. Then open WitnessWork on your iPhone once so your watch gets your progress. The watch shows this month's hours and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans, counted the same way as on your iPhone (without plans, how much a day it takes to reach your goal). On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your iPhone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Two complications can go on a watch face or in your Smart Stack: Monthly Progress shows your hours toward this month's goal, with a mark where your plans put you by today; in a round spot you can choose a ring or a gauge, with your goal at its end or a clock below, and without a goal it shows your hours alone. Up Next shows your next follow-up or plan. You can also use Siri on your watch to add time, start, pause or stop your timer, and log a mileage trip, with the same phrases as on iPhone, such as "Add time in WitnessWork" or "Log a trip in WitnessWork". Your iPhone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. The watch app needs your iPhone, so it isn't available for an Apple Watch set up with Family Setup. With an Android phone, use the Wear OS app instead.
faq_appleWatchUpNext_q: What does Up Next on my Apple Watch show?
faq_appleWatchUpNext_a: Up Next shows whichever comes first: your next follow-up or your next plan. Plans appear only if you log hours. Add the Up Next complication to a watch face or your Smart Stack: touch and hold your watch face and tap Edit, or use the Watch app on your iPhone. It's also on the watch app's home screen. A follow-up or plan stays up for 15 minutes after it starts, so you can check the address or topic when you arrive, and then the next one takes its place. A plan without a start time shows for its whole day, after that day's timed items. Missed follow-ups don't appear; find them in WitnessWork on your iPhone. Names and topics are hidden while your wrist is down or your watch is locked, because others may see your watch face. Tap Up Next to open it, then tap Directions for directions in Maps on your watch, or Start Timer to start your iPhone's service timer for a plan; the timer needs your iPhone nearby. Up Next looks two weeks ahead and keeps moving along while your iPhone is away. Changes you make on your iPhone reach your watch the next time they connect. If it's out of date, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_siri_q: Can I use Siri or Shortcuts with WitnessWork?
faq_siri_a: Yes, on iPhone and iPad with iOS 17 or later, and on the Apple Watch app. Open WitnessWork once after updating, then say "Add time in WitnessWork", "Start my timer in WitnessWork", "Pause my timer in WitnessWork", "Stop my timer in WitnessWork", "Log a trip in WitnessWork" or "Log a round trip in WitnessWork". To add time you can also say log, enter, record, track or submit, and you can say how long, like "Log two hours in WitnessWork" or "Add 30 minutes to WitnessWork". Siri knows common amounts from 15 minutes to 12 hours; for any other amount, say "Add time in WitnessWork" and Siri asks how long. Siri listens in your Siri language, which can differ from the language you chose in WitnessWork. For trips, Siri asks how far. Distances use your Mileage distance unit; for a round trip, say the one-way distance and it's doubled. Stopping the timer adds its whole minutes as an entry for today and resets it; with less than a minute, nothing is added. Time and trips are added for today, as Standard time and with the car you used last. To pick a Type or car, add the action in the Shortcuts app, where you can also run it from the Action Button or a Home Screen shortcut. Adding time and the timer need you to log hours (Regular Publishers turn on Log my hours first). Logging trips needs Track Mileage on and at least one car. On iPhone and iPad the timer changes right away, and time and trips you add with Siri are saved the next time you open WitnessWork, then reach your other devices with sync like any entry. On the watch they're sent to your iPhone like other watch entries. Siri can only use your Types, car names, distance unit and timer from WitnessWork, never contacts, notes or reports. Siri and Shortcuts aren't available on Android. If Siri doesn't recognize a phrase, open WitnessWork once, wait a minute, and check that Siri is allowed for WitnessWork in Settings. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_appleWatchSync_q: Why does my Apple Watch say Syncing with iPhone?
faq_appleWatchSync_a: Time and trips you add on your watch are sent to your iPhone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved once WitnessWork runs on your iPhone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with iPhone. Its total and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your iPhone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your iPhone. Saved entries reach your other devices with sync like any other entry. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your iPhone nearby. If the watch says the timer changed on your iPhone, check the time and try again. If your iPhone can't save an entry, the watch tells you instead of confirming it, and the time isn't added; if it asks you to update WitnessWork on your iPhone, update it and try again. If your watch stays out of date, or its complications show — after a week without an update, keep your iPhone nearby and unlocked, open WitnessWork on your iPhone, then open it on your watch. After your iPhone restarts, unlock it once before syncing. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_wearOs_q: Is there a Wear OS app?
faq_wearOs_a: Yes, for an Android phone with a watch on Wear OS 3 or later. Install WitnessWork from the Play Store on your watch, or from WitnessWork's Play Store page on your phone, then open WitnessWork on your phone once so your watch gets your progress. The watch shows this month's hours and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans, counted the same way as on your phone (without plans, how much a day it takes to reach your goal). On the watch you can add time for today with an optional Type, start and pause your phone's timer, and save the timer's time as an entry. If you don't log hours as a Kingdom Publisher, you can mark that you shared the good news this month. Add the Monthly Progress and Up Next complications to a watch face, and the Monthly Progress tile to start or pause your timer or add time with a swipe. While your timer runs, it shows on your watch face with Pause and Stop; Stop adds the timer's whole minutes as an entry for today. Allow notifications when your watch asks, so the running timer can show there. Your phone keeps your records. The watch receives your monthly progress, report status, timer, Types, car names and distance unit, and for Up Next the name, address and topic of your follow-ups and the title and place of your plans for the next two weeks. It never receives notes or other contact details, and it can't edit or delete entries. Because others may see your watch, Up Next shows "Follow Up" instead of a name on watch faces, and in the app while your wrist is down; open it to see who it is. Wear OS can't add time or log trips by voice, so use the tile or the app instead. The watch app needs your phone with WitnessWork installed.
faq_wearOsSync_q: Why does my Wear OS watch say Syncing with phone?
faq_wearOsSync_a: Time you add on your watch is sent to your phone right away when it's nearby, or the next time they connect, and saved the next time you open WitnessWork on your phone. Until then your watch shows Syncing with phone. Its total, tile and complications include that time right away, except Credit Time, which is added once your phone saves it and applies your monthly credit limit. Each entry keeps the day you added it on the watch, is saved only once even if it's sent again, and isn't brought back if you already deleted it on your phone. Starting, pausing, stopping and saving the timer need your phone nearby, even if WitnessWork isn't open on it. If the watch says the timer changed on your phone, check the time and try again. If your phone can't save an entry, the watch tells you instead of confirming it, and the time isn't added; if it asks you to update WitnessWork on your phone, update it and try again. If your watch stays out of date, or its complications show — after a week without an update, check that it's connected to your phone in your watch's companion app, keep your phone nearby, open WitnessWork on your phone, then open it on your watch. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your records out of public reports.
faq_switchingPioneer_q: How do I switch between Publisher and Auxiliary Pioneer mid-month?
faq_switchingPioneer_a: Open Settings → Profile → Status and choose what fits right now: Kingdom Publisher, Regular Auxiliary, Regular Pioneer, Special Pioneer, Circuit Overseer, or Custom. Goals and totals adjust to match. Switch back when you're done. Past months keep the time you entered, so your history stays accurate.
faq_submitReport_q: Does the app submit my service report for me?
faq_submitReport_a: WitnessWork doesn't send your report anywhere by itself. How and to whom you submit is up to you and your service committee. Until last month's report is sent, the Service Report card on Home shows a Submit row for it, so you don't send this month's report before the month is over. If you already reported another way, touch and hold that row and choose Already Submitted. Open a month's Field Service Report, choose a method from the dropdown above the Submit button, and tap Submit. You can copy a plain-text summary, share it, or hand it straight to Hourglass or NW Publisher, which opens with your hours, Credit, and Bible studies filled in for you to review and send. NW Publisher only accepts the previous month's report. WitnessWork remembers your choice; you can also change it in Settings → Profile → Submission method. Once you submit, copy, or share a report, or tap Already Submitted on last month's reminder, the report and the month's card show Sent with the date. If that was a mistake, tap Sent at the top of the report, or press and hold the month's card, and choose Mark as Not Sent; last month's reminder then comes back. Opening Hourglass or NW Publisher counts only if it opens. If your device was offline when it opened, WitnessWork asks when you come back whether the report reached it, and marks it Sent only if you choose Mark as Sent. On Android, sharing doesn't mark the report, because the share sheet can't tell whether you sent it: after sending, tap Not Sent at the top of the report and choose Mark as Sent, or tap Already Submitted on the reminder.
faq_monthReportReminders_q: Can WitnessWork remind me when my report is ready to submit?
faq_monthReportReminders_a: Yes. Go to Settings → Preferences → Plans and turn on Remind Me to Submit My Report, or tap Remind Me when the report screen offers it after you submit. On the 1st of each month you get a reminder at your Remind At time (9:00 AM unless you change it) that last month's report is ready. Tapping it opens that month's report, where you can review it and submit it with your usual method. WitnessWork never submits your report for you. There's no reminder for a month with nothing logged, or for a report you've already submitted from the report screen or marked as already submitted from the Home bell; submitting it after the reminder arrives clears it. Turning the setting on asks for notification permission, or opens your device settings if you've declined before. The reminder is worked out on your device from your own records and isn't sent anywhere. Each device schedules its own reminder, so open WitnessWork during the month to keep it current; if you submit on another device, open WitnessWork on this one so it knows. On Android, the system may deliver it a few minutes late to save battery. If it doesn't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. Last month's report is also listed in the Home bell until you submit it, even with notifications off. If it still doesn't work, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_remainingHours_q: How do I see how many hours I have left this month or year?
faq_remainingHours_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. The Month sub-screen shows time so far and hours left for the current month. Pioneers can switch to the Year sub-screen to see annual goal progress, time so far, remaining hours, and a per-month breakdown comparing actual hours to plan.
faq_goalPacing_q: How can I tell if I'm ahead or behind on my hour goal?
faq_goalPacing_a: Open the Progress tab from the bottom bar. On the Month view, the report shows how much is left and how many days are left, and the line under it shows whether you're ahead or behind your plans. The Daily Pace card shows how much a day it takes to reach your goal; add it with Edit Cards if it isn't there. Pioneers can switch to the Year view, where the Service Year Pace chart shows how far ahead or behind your Annual Goal you are today, and each month's bar shows how that month did against its goal. The Year Pace card shows how much a month you need for the rest of the service year.
faq_dailyPace_q: How much do I need each day to reach my goal?
faq_dailyPace_a: Add the Daily Pace card on the Progress tab's Month view (tap Edit Cards, then Add Cards); it's there by default for roles with a monthly goal. It takes what's left of your monthly goal and divides it by the days left in the month after today, the same count the month's report shows as days left. For example, with 25 of 50 hours done and 20 days left, it shows 1.3 hours a day (the figure rounds up slightly, so keeping to it is always enough). On the last day of the month, it shows everything that's left as today's amount. Make the card wide to also see about how much that is a week. Credit time counts up to its monthly limit, as on your report, and your plans aren't counted; the Projected Month card shows where your plans put you. Once you reach your goal, the card says so. For a past month it shows what you averaged a day, and for a future month what each day would need. It doesn't appear when the month has no goal. For the year, the Year Pace card does the same with your annual goal, spread over the months left in the service year.
faq_serviceYearPace_q: How do I read the Service Year Pace chart?
faq_serviceYearPace_a: Open the Progress tab and switch to Year. If your status has an Annual Goal, such as regular pioneer, the Service Year Pace card appears below your milestones. The dashed gray line is where your Annual Goal puts you by the end of each month. It is built from each month's own goal, so a mid-year appointment or an auxiliary pioneer month changes it, but a Monthly Goal you changed yourself does not. The green line is your time so far, counted the same way as your Service Report, including each month's credit limit. The dashed green line adds the time you have planned. The faint line is last service year, shown when you logged time in it, and the number at its end is last year's total. If a line runs well past your Annual Goal, the space above the goal is drawn on a compressed (logarithmic) scale so the months below stay readable. Press and hold the chart, then slide your finger, to see any month's totals. "Ahead of pace" compares your time with where the goal line is today. Below the card, each month has a bar: solid for logged time, lighter for credit time, and striped for plans, with a tick at that month's goal. The key above the months explains these marks, and the Hours and vs Goal columns give the numbers. Every bar uses the same scale, so you can compare months. Without an Annual Goal you see the month bars but not the chart. If a month looks wrong, press and hold it to change its status or goal. The chart is drawn on your device from your own entries and isn't shared.
faq_timeFormat_q: Can I display time as "1h 30m" instead of "1.5"?
faq_timeFormat_a: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats and choose a Duration Format. Both formats are available everywhere time is shown.
faq_weekStart_q: Can I start the week on Monday instead of Sunday?
faq_weekStart_a: Yes. Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats → Start of Week lets you choose the first day of the week. The change applies to the calendar, schedule, and any other weekly views.
faq_darkMode_q: Can I force dark mode or light mode?
faq_darkMode_a: Yes. Open Settings → Personalization → Color Scheme and pick Device, Dark, or Light. The app will stop following your phone's setting and use the one you choose.
faq_appIcon_q: Can I change the app's icon?
faq_appIcon_a: Alternate app icons are a Supporter perk on iOS. Open Settings → Personalization → App Icon and choose an alternate. Alternate app icons are unavailable on Android.
faq_reorderHome_q: How do I rearrange or hide the sections on Home?
faq_reorderHome_a: Press and hold a section, then choose Edit Home Screen, or press and hold an empty space on Home. The sections start to jiggle. Hold a section and drag it to move it; on iPad, sections can move between the two columns. Tap the gray minus at a section's top corner to hide it (tap Undo if you didn't mean to). To show a hidden section again, tap Add Sections at the top; it comes back first on Home. Tap Done, or tap an empty space, when you're finished; on Android, the back button works too. A section with nothing to show right now, like Approaching Conversations when you have no follow-ups today, appears as an outline while you edit, so you can still move or hide it. Getting Started stays at the top until you finish or close it. Some sections depend on your role or device: Timer appears for roles that log time, Mileage when mileage tracking is on, and Service Year Summary on iPad with an annual goal. With Reduce Motion on, sections stay still while you edit. You can also show, hide, and reorder sections in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. Hiding a section never deletes your data. Your layout is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on.
faq_reorderTabs_q: Can I change the order of the tabs?
faq_reorderTabs_a: Yes. Open Settings → Preferences → Tab Order and use the up and down arrows beside each tab, or long-press a tab's name to move it to the top or bottom. The new order applies right away to the bottom bar on phones and the sidebar on tablets, on iOS and Android. Tabs can be reordered but not hidden. WitnessWork still opens on Home, and Progress only appears for roles that log hours; it keeps its place in your order if you change roles. On iPad, Command-number keyboard shortcuts follow your order too. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on; it doesn't change any of your records. To go back, move the tabs back to Home, Contacts, Progress, Schedule. If the order doesn't update, restart the app and use Still need help? below.
faq_progressCards_q: How do I choose what's on my Progress screen?
faq_progressCards_a: Each tab on Progress (Month, Year, and All-time) has its own cards under its summary, and you choose them separately. To change a tab's cards, press and hold any card; it lifts and the cards start to jiggle, and you can drag it straight away. You can also tap Edit Cards under your cards, or the grid button at the top. While the cards jiggle, drag a card to move it, tap the gray minus at its top corner to remove it (tap Undo if you didn't mean to), and drag the curved handle at its bottom corner to make it small or wide; tapping the handle switches sizes too. Cards that come in only one size have no handle. Tap Add Cards at the top to see every card that tab offers. Month has Daily Pace, Studies, Days Out, Visits, Credit, Weeks, Projected Month, Service Year, Year Pace, Streak, Lifetime, and Days. Year has Service Year Pace, Needed a Month, Average, Best Month, Last Year, Days Out, Months Out, Studies, and Visits for the service year shown. All-time has Best Year, Average, Best Month, Days Out, Months Out, Studies, and Visits across all your records. The Days list on Month can show every day of the month or, when compact, only the latest few in a short list that scrolls on its own; drag its handle down or up to switch. To lift the Days list, hold its title rather than a day, since each day has its own menu. Tap Done, or tap the summary at the top, when you're finished. Each tab's summary (the month's report, the service year's total, or your lifetime hours) and the lists of months and years always stay. Some cards only appear when they apply: Daily Pace and Projected Month need a monthly goal, Year Pace, Service Year Pace, and Needed a Month need an annual goal, Credit needs a role whose report counts hours, hour cards on Year need a role that logs hours, Streak needs streaks turned on, and Mileage needs mileage tracking. With Reduce Motion on, the cards stay still while you edit. Removing a card never deletes your time or reports. Your cards are a preference, so they're included in backups and sync with your other devices when sync is on. To start over on a tab, tap Edit Cards there, then Reset Cards.
faq_progressStats_q: What do the Year and All-time cards count?
faq_progressStats_a: On Year, time counts as each month's report counts it: credit time counts up to that month's limit. Average on Year runs from your first month with time to the last month that's ended; the month under way joins only while it's the only one. Last Year compares this service year so far with last service year at the same point, or the whole of both once the year is over. On All-time, time counts as you logged it, before monthly credit limits, the same as your lifetime hours and Year by Year. Average on All-time covers the service years that have ended, or the one under way if it's your first. Months Out counts the months you shared in the ministry, with or without hours, starting from your first record; the month under way counts once you've shared in it, and it's never shown as missed. On All-time it also shows your longest run of months in a row. Studies counts each contact you marked a Bible study with once, and shows the most any one month had, which is that month's figure for your report. Contacts you've deleted aren't counted. Visits counts visits where you talked with someone; not-at-homes are counted separately. Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so Studies and Visits leave them out.
