Everything is worked out on this device from your own records, and nothing new is stored or shared. If a figure looks wrong, check the month's report and the visits on the contact; you can contact support from the Help Center, leaving out names and notes.
faq_timerRounding_q: Why was my timer rounded to the nearest 5 minutes?
faq_timerRounding_a: That was old behavior. Recent versions save the exact stopwatch time when you stop the timer, with no rounding. If you're still seeing 5-minute rounding, update the app to the latest version.
faq_addNotesToTime_q: Can I add notes to a time entry?
faq_addNotesToTime_a: Yes. When you add or edit a time entry, you can attach a note (e.g. "cart witnessing" or "cut short"). You can also tag entries with categories so similar entries stay grouped in your time reports.
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_q: I'm a special pioneer, why is the app showing me an annual goal?
faq_specialPioneerAnnual_a: Special pioneers don't have an annual goal by default. If yours appears, open Settings → Profile and set Annual Goal to No. Your monthly goal stays in place and the annual bar on the Progress tab's Year sub-screen will be hidden.
faq_ldcCreditCap_q: Are LDC and other credit hours included in my totals?
faq_ldcCreditCap_a: Yes. Credit hours count toward your monthly hour total. For the service-year total, up to 55 credit hours per month are counted, in line with the branch's published cap. Anything above the cap is still kept on the entry but doesn't roll into the annual total.
faq_timezoneShift_q: Will my entries, plans, or reminders move if I travel to another time zone?
faq_timezoneShift_a: Entries and plans stay on their day. As of the April 2026 update, every time entry and plan is anchored to its calendar date independent of time zone, so traveling or crossing a daylight-saving boundary won't move them to a different day. Older entries created before that update are migrated automatically the first time you open the new version. When you open WitnessWork after changing time zones, Home, Schedule, and Progress switch to the new zone's today, and reminders set for a time of day, such as a Plan's reminder or the reminders to log time, plan next week, or submit your report, move to that same time where you are. Follow-ups keep their exact moment, so they show at the matching local time. If you ever spot an entry on the wrong day, please send a bug report and we'll take a look.
faq_scheduleViews_q: How do I plan across months or see my whole service year?
faq_scheduleViews_a: The Schedule tab has two views; switch between them with the buttons at the top. Month shows your weeks as one calendar you scroll through without stopping at the end of a month, so you can plan this month and next side by side. The month you're reading stays bright and the others fade back, and the card above the calendar shows that month's goal: logged and planned time (striped) against your goal, the time you've logged, and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans. Tap it for goal coverage, schedule pace, and the Assistant. Each day shows the time you planned, or the time you logged once you log some. Tap a day to see or change it, or touch and hold it to add time or plan it. Year shows the twelve months of the service year (September through August), each day colored like the calendar, under the same card for the whole service year: logged and planned time (striped) against your annual goal if you have one, the time you've logged, and whether you're ahead of or behind your plans. Tap a month, or pinch outward, to zoom into it; pinch inward in Month to zoom back out. A labeled line marks where one service year ends and the next begins; tap it to see that year. Use the arrows or swipe to change years, and tap Today to come back. Both views only show what's already in your records; changing views doesn't share anything.
faq_planDetails_q: What's on a Plan's page, and how do I change a Plan?
faq_planDetails_a: Tap a day on the Schedule tab, then tap one of its Plans, or tap a Plan on Home, to open it. Its page shows the date, when it starts and ends (with the next day's date if it runs past midnight) or Anytime for a Plan with no set time, how long it is, its Type, how often it repeats, the place, and the note; tap the place to open it in Maps. To change the Plan, tap Edit (the pencil). For a recurring plan, saving asks whether the change is for only this date, this and future dates, or all dates. More (•••) holds Duplicate, Log as Time, Open in Maps, Copy Address, Copy Note, and Delete. Duplicate opens a new Plan with the same details; a one-time Plan's copy starts on the same day next week, and you can change the date before you save. With Buddies, the page also lists who you invited and how each answered, plus anyone who asked to join, with Invite. Tap Invite Buddies to invite someone right away while the Plan is still ahead; they get the date, time, title, location, and note. To take someone off, use Edit. For a Plan you joined through a buddy's invitation, the page shows who organized it and your answer. Switch between Going and Can't Make It anytime until the Plan ends: Can't Make It takes the Plan off your schedule, and Going puts it back. After the Plan, you can still open it, with its note and photos, for a month, but no longer change your answer.
faq_editRecurringPlan_q: Can I edit or delete a single occurrence of a recurring plan?
faq_editRecurringPlan_a: Yes. On the Schedule tab, tap the day, then tap the plan to open it. To change only that date, tap Edit (the pencil), make your changes, save, and choose Only this date. Changing the Type, title, location, or Notify Me reminder for one date turns that date into its own one-time plan. To remove only that date, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Your recurring plan stays intact for every other day.
faq_awayDay_q: How do I mark a day I'm not going out without breaking my recurring plan?
faq_awayDay_a: Tap a plan on that day in the Schedule tab to open it, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan. Do this for each plan on that day. Only that day is removed, and a recurring plan keeps going from the next day forward. To go out at a different time that day instead, tap Edit, change it, and choose Only this date when you save.
faq_multiplePlansOneDay_q: Can I plan more than one activity on the same day?
faq_multiplePlansOneDay_a: Yes. A day can hold as many plans as you like, one-time, recurring, or both, like field service every Friday morning and a Bible study every Friday evening. Every plan on a day adds up: the day's planned time on the Schedule calendar, the time left to plan, and your projected total all count each one. To add another plan, tap the day on the Schedule tab, then tap + next to Plans. To skip a recurring plan on one day, open it, tap More (•••), then Delete → Delete This Plan; your other days stay the same. To change it for one day only, tap Edit and choose Only this date when you save. One-time plans used to replace a day's recurring plans. When you updated, days where that happened were set to skip the recurring plan, so your totals didn't change. If a day shows more time than you expect, tap it and delete the plan you don't need. Plans stay on your device, sync between your devices if you turned sync on, and only their day, time, and length are shared with your buddies if you use Buddies.
faq_planJustHours_q: Can I plan hours without picking a time?
faq_planJustHours_a: Yes. On the Plan form, tap the How long? button next to the date. Choose Just hours to plan the hours for that day without a time, or Time span to pick when you start and finish; the hours add up for you. New Plans open in whichever one you used last, so your usual way is ready next time. A Just hours Plan shows Anytime on your Schedule and counts toward your goals like any other Plan. With Notify Me on, it reminds you at 8:00 AM that day instead of before a start time. Buddies you invite see the day and how long, with no time. To give it a time later, edit the Plan and switch to Time span. If another of your devices still runs an older version of WitnessWork, it shows the Plan at noon until it updates.
faq_planFirstMonth_q: Can WitnessWork plan my month for me?
faq_planFirstMonth_a: Yes. During setup, if you log hours and have a monthly goal, you get a quick preview of the Assistant: pick the days you usually go out and it spreads your goal across those days for this month, or next month if fewer than seven days are left. This month's plan starts on the 1st, so the days that have already passed get plans too: log the time you already spent on them. Days you've already logged time on are left alone. Tap any day to change its plan with the slider, or to plan a day yourself. Tap Add to my schedule to save them as plans on the Schedule tab, where you can change or delete any of them, or tap I'll plan later to continue without plans. The weekdays you didn't pick become off days, so the Assistant won't suggest plans on them; change this anytime in Settings → Preferences → Plans → Availability. After setup, you plan on the Schedule tab by tapping any day, and the Assistant there suggests plans whenever you're short of your goal. Plans are saved with your other records and don't count toward your report; log the time you actually spend. Kingdom Publishers who don't log hours, and anyone without a monthly goal, skip this step but can still add plans from the Schedule tab.
faq_importContacts_q: Can I import contacts from my phone's address book?
faq_importContacts_a: Not at this time. Contacts are entered manually in WitnessWork. This keeps your ministry contacts private and avoids accidentally pulling in personal contacts.
faq_importOtherApps_q: Can I import data from MyTime, Ministry Assistant, or another app?
faq_importOtherApps_a: MyTime backups are supported. In MyTime, go to More → Settings → Backup and email yourself a backup, then save the attached .mytimedb file on your device. On Android, send it from MyTime on your iPhone and download the attachment on your Android phone. Open Settings → MyTime Import, or choose From MyTime during setup, choose that file, and review the preview before importing. Other apps' backup formats are not automatically supported. If you can export readable text, Notes Import may help bring it in with Scribe AI on supported devices when available. Review its proposed records and warnings before saving. WitnessWork JSON backups belong in Settings → Backup & Restore instead.
faq_backupRestore_q: How do I back up and restore my data?
faq_backupRestore_a: For an automatic, end-to-end encrypted backup, turn on Backup in Settings → Account; see "What is WitnessWork Backup?". For a backup file, open Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup or Restore From Backup to export or restore a JSON backup on iOS or Android. To restore, choose the witness-work-backup.json file you saved with Create Backup. On a new device, you can also choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen; restoring there finishes setup with your restored profile. Backups include service records, plans, contacts, visits, categories, mileage, your pet, profile, and shared preferences. A restore replaces the included local data; older backups may omit categories or profile, which are kept as they are, and contacts in older backups keep their custom field values. A backup made with a newer version of WitnessWork can't be restored until you update WitnessWork on this device. If some items in a backup can't be read, the rest is restored and WitnessWork tells you how many items were left out. Device identity, sync settings, data protection mode, analytics consent, and onboarding progress stay local to this device. Photo files are not embedded in JSON backups. For iCloud or Google Drive photos, enable photo sync separately; Cloud Sync doesn't carry photos yet. A backup restores on iPhone or Android, so it can move your records from one to the other; to keep both in step instead, use Cloud Sync (see “What is Cloud Sync?”). Save a current backup before restoring and keep it in a private location; it can contain householder details. Use the Help Center’s private support option for recovery help.
faq_shareAddress_q: How do I get directions to a contact?
faq_shareAddress_a: Open the contact and tap their address. You'll be offered Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze depending on what's installed. You can also pin a contact's location without an address, which is useful for areas where street numbers don't exist.
faq_manualPin_q: My pin is in the wrong place. Can I move it?
faq_manualPin_a: Yes. Open the contact's address screen and drag the pin to the correct spot. You can also place a pin without an address at all, which is helpful in areas without precise geolocation data.
faq_profilePic_q: Can I add a photo to a contact?
faq_profilePic_a: Yes. Open a contact, tap the avatar, and pick a photo from your library or take a new one. This is especially handy when contacts share names or when a photo helps you spot the right door.
faq_dismissContact_q: How do I hide a contact without deleting them?
faq_dismissContact_a: Open the contact and tap "Dismiss." You'll pick how long to dismiss them for (1 week, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months, or 1 year). The contact disappears from your active lists for that period and then comes back automatically when the time is up. If notifications are enabled, you'll also get a reminder when they reappear, so dismissed contacts won't quietly slip through the cracks. You can find or restore dismissed contacts at any time from the link at the bottom of your Contacts list, the ••• menu in Contacts, or Settings → Dismissed Contacts.
faq_deleteContact_q: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a contact?
faq_deleteContact_a: Touch and hold a contact in Contacts or on the map, or open it and tap More (•••), then choose Archive or Delete Permanently…. In Select mode, use Archive or Delete at the bottom. Swiping a contact from the right archives it. Archiving hides the contact and keeps it and every conversation logged with them. Restore it within 90 days from Settings → More → Recover Contacts; after that its details are removed. Deleting permanently erases the contact, every conversation logged with them, and their photos, on this device and on devices that sync with it through Cloud Sync, iCloud Sync, or Google Drive Sync. It can't be undone, so WitnessWork asks first and offers Archive Instead. To delete a contact you already archived, touch and hold it in Recover Contacts and choose Delete Permanently…. With data protection mode on there's no Archive: removing a contact always deletes it. To hide a contact only for a while, use Dismiss For instead. Backup files you saved earlier still contain deleted contacts. If you deleted one by mistake, it can only come back by restoring a backup made before the delete, which replaces your current data, so create a fresh backup first. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_contactsFollowUpFilter_q: How do I find contacts with no follow-up planned?
faq_contactsFollowUpFilter_a: In Contacts, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top, tap Add filter, choose Follow-up, then pick a value and tap Apply. Upcoming shows contacts with a follow-up that's still ahead and that you haven't visited since. None upcoming shows everyone else, so you can find people you haven't planned a return visit for. Missed shows contacts whose follow-up passed more than 4 hours ago, within the last 30 days, with no visit since: the same people as your missed follow-up reminders. Dismissed follow-ups don't count. To see who's next, choose Next follow-up under Sort: each contact then shows when their follow-up is due in place of their last visit. The soonest follow-up comes first with Descending, the latest with Ascending, then missed follow-ups, and contacts with none go last. Other sorts, like Bible Study, Date added, or City, show the value they sort by in the same place. Follow-up filters work on iOS and Android, apply to the list and the map alike, and can be part of a saved view. They're worked out on your device, and nothing is shared. If a contact appears where you don't expect, open their most recent visit and check its follow-up date, or whether a later visit already answered it. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_contactStalenessFilter_q: How do I see which contacts are due for a visit?
faq_contactStalenessFilter_a: Below the search field in Contacts, tap a chip to show only contacts in that group: Stale, This month, This week, or Never contacted. Each chip shows how many active contacts it holds, and its color matches the contact's pin on the map. Swipe the chips sideways to see them all. Tap the chip again, or tap All, to show everyone. The same chips sit at the top of the map, where they count only contacts with a location and filter the pins; they tuck away while you move the map, so tap the Contacts title to bring them back. To change their order, touch a chip, pause briefly, then drag it along the row; All stays first. The order is a preference, so it's included in backups and syncs with your other devices when sync is on. Groups are based on your most recent visit, and "Not at homes" count as visits. To change when a contact moves between groups, or the colors, tap the info button at the end of the chips (on the map, the legend button) and then the pencil. A chip adds a filter you can also see and remove in Sort & Filter, and it applies to the list and the map alike. Dismissed contacts aren't counted. Nothing is shared; the groups are worked out on your device.
faq_reportBug_q: How do I report a bug or request a feature?
faq_reportBug_a: Use the buttons below to report a bug or request a feature. Include the steps to reproduce it, what you expected, your device and operating-system version, and the WitnessWork version shown under Still need help?. Remove private contact details, notes, account IDs, and Buddies Codes or invite links from public reports and screenshots. For backup or other sensitive problems, use the private email link in Still need help? instead. Source code, the Privacy Policy, and Terms of Use are under Settings → About.
faq_translations_q: Which languages does WitnessWork support, and how do I change or report a translation?
faq_translations_a: WitnessWork is available in 19 languages: Arabic, Bemba, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Kinyarwanda, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Spanish, Swahili, Ukrainian, and Vietnamese. It follows your device's language by default (Device Default). To pick another, open Settings and change Language at the top; WitnessWork restarts in that language. You can also set a language for WitnessWork alone in your phone's settings: on iPhone and iPad, Settings → Apps → WitnessWork → Language (shown once your device has more than one preferred language); on Android 13 or later, Settings → Apps → WitnessWork → Language. With Device Default, WitnessWork follows that choice, and a language picked inside WitnessWork takes priority. If your language isn't supported, the app shows English. Some text is drawn by your phone, so it follows your phone's language instead: alert buttons, date pickers, share sheets, and the widget gallery. On iPhone and iPad, the explanations in permission requests (location, camera, microphone, and others) are still in English. Translations are made with AI, so a word or phrase may sometimes be off, especially terms Jehovah's Witnesses use in a particular way. To report one, use the email link in Still need help? and include your language, the screen, the text you see, and what it should say. A screenshot helps; cover names, addresses, and notes first. Corrections arrive in a later app update. There is no longer a volunteer translation project to join.
faq_arabic_q: How does WitnessWork work in Arabic and right to left?
faq_arabic_a: Choose العربية under Settings → Language, or set your phone to Arabic and keep Device Default. WitnessWork restarts and reads right to left: screens, menus, swipe actions, progress bars, and charts are mirrored, and back arrows point the other way. Numbers show in Arabic-Indic digits (٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩), and months use the names in Jehovah's Witnesses' Arabic publications, such as تشرين الأول (أكتوبر). When you enter hours, goals, or mileage, you can type Arabic-Indic or Latin digits. Names, phone numbers, addresses, and notes stay exactly as you typed them. Date order, the clock, and the first day of the week follow your Format Region in Settings → Preferences → Region & Formats: choose Middle East (Arabic) there for weeks that start on Saturday, or leave it on Auto (Device) to follow your phone. Widgets and the Apple Watch and Wear OS apps follow WitnessWork's language and direction after the app has opened once. Searching contacts and help finds Arabic words with or without vowel marks. Your records are stored the same way in every language, so switching to another language, or back, changes only how they are shown.
faq_becomeSupporter_q: What do I get as a supporter?
faq_becomeSupporter_a: An active Supporter subscription gives you the Supporter badge, custom accent colors and Plan Today's Route, which puts the day's follow-ups and plans in the shortest driving order, plus Device Sync, and alternate app icons on iOS. Device Sync is Cloud Sync, the only option that syncs live, even between iPhone and Android, or iCloud Sync on iOS and Google Drive Sync on Android. Supporters also get a larger Scribe AI allowance for Notes Import on iOS and Android where it is available; the current free and Supporter allowances appear in Help and on the support screen. Core features remain free, including contact filters, sorting and saved views, and Buddies when available; Supporters can also choose each buddy's color. A one-time Tip gives Donor recognition but does not activate Supporter features.
faq_stillFree_a: Yes — and always will be. Every core feature stays free for everyone. Supporting is completely optional; it helps fund ongoing development and unlocks a few personal touches as a thank-you.
faq_stopSupporting_q: What happens if I stop supporting?
faq_stopSupporting_a: To stop, open Settings → Manage subscription and choose Cancel or change subscription, or cancel in your App Store or Google Play subscriptions. Supporter access continues until the end of the period you've paid for, and your existing data and local backups remain available. After that, sync pauses while Supporter access is unavailable. If sync was on, it resumes when access returns; an explicit choice to turn it off stays off. Photo sync follows its own setting. Your accent color and app icon return to the defaults, but your choices are kept for when you support again. Check Settings → Sync for the current status. If you only need a break, you can pause instead.
faq_pauseSupport_q: Can I pause my support instead of cancelling?
faq_pauseSupport_a: Yes. Open Settings → Manage subscription. On iPhone and iPad, choose to pause payments for 1, 3, or 6 months. The pause starts when your current period ends. You aren't charged during it, and Supporter features stay on, including sync, your accent color, and app icon. Payments then resume automatically at the same amount on the date shown, and you can still cancel anytime in your App Store subscriptions. You can pause once every 12 months; the pause dates are saved with your settings so your other devices respect them. On Android, choose Pause in Google Play to pause a monthly subscription for 1 to 3 months. Supporter features such as the badge and accent color pause too, then return automatically with your settings kept, and you can resume early in Google Play. Pause options don't appear during a free trial, a payment problem, a Family Sharing subscription, or within 12 months of your last pause. If a pause fails, nothing changes; try again later or manage your subscription in your store. For anything else, use Still need help? to contact support privately.
faq_acceptDonations_a: As a brother in the hall, I consider it a privilege to be able to use my skills to help others in the congregation. Although free to everyone, developing, running, and maintaining this application, unfortunately costs a significant amount of money and time. I view donating as similar to how one might pay for another's gas after going in service with them - it's a loving gesture that goes greatly appreciated.
faq_donationsUsedFor_q: What are the donations used for?
faq_donationsUsedFor_a: Your donation helps keeps this app running! There are costs with purchasing real devices as development equipment, paying for location API service fees, build service API fees, app store fees, and opportunity cost of my many hours spent developing this app. Each piece of support is greatly appreciated!
faq_whatsNew_q: Where can I see what changed in the latest update?
faq_findNavigation_q: Where are Map, Buddies, and Settings?
faq_findNavigation_a: The bottom bar shows Home, Schedule, Contacts, and Progress, with Add beside them for logging time, creating a Plan, or adding a contact. Progress and Add Time appear when your role logs hours. Map is inside Contacts: tap the map button beside the Contacts title, and WitnessWork opens the view you used last. Buddies, when available on iOS, opens from the Buddies button at the top of Schedule. View Report at the top of Progress opens the Service Report for the month you're viewing. Tap your profile picture at the top left of any main screen for Profile (your role, time served, and stats), Settings, Support, and Help Center; on a wide tablet layout, Settings also stays in the sidebar. If you hid the sidebar, tap Show sidebar in the page header to bring it back. If you turned on Hide Donate Heart, Support is left out of that menu and stays in Settings. Your contacts, plans, and records are unchanged; only where you find them moved. If something still seems missing, update the app, then use Still need help? below.
faq_tabletSidebar_q: How do I resize or hide the sidebar on my tablet?
faq_tabletSidebar_a: On a wide tablet window on iOS or Android, drag the small bar halfway down the sidebar's right edge to resize it. Narrowing the sidebar hides destination names and leaves their icons; widen it to show the names again. Tap Hide sidebar beside WitnessWork (at the top of the icon-only sidebar) to hide navigation completely. Tap Show sidebar in the page header to restore your last saved width. Your width and visibility are saved on this device across app restarts; they are not synced or included in ministry backups, and resizing does not change your records. The sidebar needs a window at least 1,000 points wide and a supported text size. In a narrower window or with very large text, the bottom bar returns automatically; widen the window or rotate to landscape to use the sidebar again. Screen reader users can adjust the Resize sidebar control to increase or decrease its width. If the navigation still seems missing, restart the app and use Still need help? below; keep contact details and other private data out of public reports.
faq_whatsNew_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → What's New, for a summary of recent changes. Big updates also open a short tour the first time you launch after updating. If you choose Later, the notification bell keeps a shortcut to it, and What's New has a button to take the tour again.
faq_notificationsTray_q: What's in the bell on Home?
faq_notificationsTray_a: The bell at the top of Home collects reminders and updates, so they wait there instead of piling up on Home when you open the app. You'll find things like last month's Service Report, a pending time rollover, backup and data protection reminders, missed Follow-ups, reminders that already went off, Buddies activity (where Buddies is available), ready Notes Imports, and What's New. The red badge counts items you haven't seen yet. News from your buddies, like a buddy's new badge or a reaction to yours, sits at the bottom under From your buddies and never adds to that number; a small dot on the bell means some of it is new. Tap an item to act on it, tap X to dismiss it, or tap Clear All. Invitations and requests still waiting for your answer stay until you respond. A dismissed item doesn't come back. Which items you've seen or dismissed is remembered on this device only.
faq_shareApp_q: How do I share WitnessWork with a friend?
faq_shareApp_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings → Share WitnessWork. Pick Android or iPhone, and your friend can scan the code with their phone's camera to open WitnessWork in Google Play or the App Store. Share Link sends a message with both store links, so it works for anyone. WitnessWork is free on both. The message only contains the store links — nothing about you or your records. If a code won't scan, turn up your screen's brightness or use Share Link instead.
faq_android_a: Yes. WitnessWork is back on Google Play, and it's free. Time and reports, the timer, contacts and follow-ups, plans, the map (with Google Maps), mileage, reminders, and backups all work on Android. Buddies works on Android too, including with buddies on iPhone. Supporters can keep their devices in sync with Cloud Sync, which also syncs with an iPhone, or with Google Drive Sync between Android devices. A few features rely on Apple services and stay on iPhone and iPad: iCloud Sync, widgets, Live Activities, and app icons. Notes Import with Scribe AI is rolling out on Android. To move to a new phone on either platform, use Set Up Another Device on the old phone (Settings → Account); with Cloud Sync, the new phone gets your records without a restore step, or it offers to restore your Backup if you turned it on in Settings → Account. You can also create a backup file (Settings → Backup & Restore → Create Backup), copy it to the new phone, then choose From a backup file on the “Pick up where you left off” setup screen. Between Android devices you can also choose From Google Drive there. Keep backup files private; they can contain householder details.
faq_dataPrivacy_q: Is my data private and secure?
faq_dataPrivacy_a: Yes. WitnessWork has no sign-up and no ads, and your records live on your device. Anything that leaves it is encrypted or anonymized, so it isn't tied to you. Your account is anonymous: no email, phone number, or password. If you turn on Backup (Settings → Account), WitnessWork's server keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of your records that only your devices can read, not WitnessWork; it's off unless you turn it on. Cloud Sync keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of each device's data on WitnessWork's server that only your devices can read. iCloud Sync and Google Drive Sync go straight to your own account over an encrypted connection, never through WitnessWork's servers; on iPhone and iPad, turning on Apple's Advanced Data Protection makes iCloud end-to-end encrypted. Buddies is end-to-end encrypted, so only you and your buddies can read what you share. A shared contact travels inside its link and isn't stored by WitnessWork. Notes Import sends your notes over an encrypted connection to Zero Data Retention providers that don't store them, and route planning sends only map coordinates. Usage statistics are anonymous counts that never include names, contacts, reports, or notes; turn them off anytime in Settings → Preferences → Share Anonymous Usage Statistics. Supporter purchases use a random identifier, not your name or email. Backup files you export are yours, so keep them somewhere private; they can include householder details. WitnessWork deletes its own temporary copies of exported backups, shared contact files, and picked photos the next time it starts and when you permanently delete householder data. For privacy questions, use the private support link in the Help Center.
openSourceLicenses_description: WitnessWork is built with {{packages}} open-source packages. Thank you to the people who maintain them. Tap a package to see its license and source.
faq_about_q: Where are the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and open-source licenses?
faq_about_a: Tap your profile picture, then Settings, and scroll to About. It links to the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, and WitnessWork's source code. On devices where Notes Import is available, it also links to the OpenRouter ZDR policy that covers notes you send to Scribe AI. Open Source Licenses lists every open-source package WitnessWork is built with, along with its version, license, and author; tap a package to open its page, which shows the full license and source. Search by package name, license, or author. Long-press any link to copy or share it.
faq_debugTools_a: Debugging Tools helps troubleshoot problems with support. Turn it on in Settings → Advanced; it applies only to the device you turn it on for, on iOS and Android. It adds a Tools tab with diagnostic, test-data, and repair actions, shows extra technical details on some screens, and turns on more detailed diagnostic logging. Some Tools actions add sample data or permanently delete data, so only use them when support asks, and back up first under Settings → Backup & Restore. Turning the switch on or off doesn't change your data; turn it off to hide the Tools tab and details again.
faq_backupRecovery_q: My backup looks unreadable or my restored records are missing. What should I do?
faq_backupRecovery_a: A WitnessWork backup is structured JSON for the app to read, so it does not look like a printable Service Report. Keep the original file unchanged and restore it through Settings → Backup & Restore → Restore From Backup. If records are missing, preserve the original backup and create a separate backup of the device's current data before trying another restore. Email support with the app version and what happened; arrange any file sharing privately. Backup files can contain contact details and notes, so keep them out of public bug reports.
faq_accountBackup_a: WitnessWork Backup keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of your service records, time, plans, contacts, visits and notes, categories, mileage, profile, and shared settings on WitnessWork's server, so you can restore them on a new phone, on iPhone or Android. It's free for everyone and off until you turn it on: go to Settings → Account and turn on Back Up to WitnessWork. It then backs up when your data changes, when you leave the app, and at least once a day; Back Up Now backs up right away. Settings → Account shows when it last backed up and lists one backup for each of your devices. Photos aren't included (contact photos and photos in notes), and neither are this phone's own settings like data protection mode, sync settings, or analytics consent. A backup can be up to 20 MB, and an account can keep backups from up to 8 devices. It works alongside Cloud Sync, iCloud Sync, and Google Drive Sync, which keep your devices in step; the backup is a snapshot for moving to a new phone, including between iPhone and Android, or recovering a lost one.
faq_accountBackupPrivacy_a: No. Your phone encrypts the backup with a key made from your account key before it leaves the phone, and only your devices have that key. WitnessWork's server stores the encrypted backup, its size, when it was uploaded, and a random number for each device, never your name, email, or device name, and it can't read any of your records. That's also why no one can recover your backup for you: if you lose every phone that uses your account and your recovery key, your backup can't be opened by anyone, including us. Keep your recovery key somewhere safe (Settings → Account → Show Recovery Key).
faq_accountBackupRestore_q: How do I restore my backup on a new phone?
faq_accountBackupRestore_a: Install WitnessWork on the new phone and bring your account over. With your old phone, use Set Up Another Device: during setup, tap "I already use WitnessWork", then From your other phone, and scan the code on the old phone (Settings → Account → Set Up Another Device). Without your old phone, use your recovery key: Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key. The new phone then offers to restore your backup. When your other devices use Cloud Sync and are at least as up to date as the backup, your records arrive through Cloud Sync instead. If it has no records yet, tap Restore. If it already has records, choose Combine to keep them and add the backup's, or Replace to use only the backup. Restoring combines every device's backup on your account. You can also restore later from Settings → Account → Restore from Backup. A backup from a newer version of WitnessWork is left out until you update, and one that can't be read is skipped; the app tells you. When iCloud Keychain or Google's backup brings your account back on a reinstalled phone, the app offers your backup once. Afterwards, turn on Backup on the new phone too.
faq_accountBackupDelete_q: How do I delete my backup, and how long is it kept?
faq_accountBackupDelete_a: Go to Settings → Account. Tap one device's backup to delete just that one, or tap Delete Backup to delete every device's backup; both also turn off backup on this phone, and they're gone from the server right away. Other devices with backup on back up again the next time they're opened, or within about 20 minutes while they're open. Turning off Back Up to WitnessWork asks whether to delete this phone's backup too. A device's backup that hasn't been updated for 400 days is deleted automatically. Delete My Buddies Data (Buddies Settings) also deletes your backup, because it gives you a new account and recovery key; with backup on, the next backup goes to your new account. If deleting fails because you're offline, nothing changes; try again when you're connected.
faq_cloudSync_a: Cloud Sync keeps your records the same on all your devices, including between an iPhone and an Android phone. Each device that uses it keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of its data on WitnessWork's server, and your other devices on Cloud Sync combine those copies, usually within seconds while the app is open. It's the default for devices that haven't chosen a sync option. Open Settings → Sync to see which option this device uses, turn sync off, or switch to iCloud (Google Drive on Android). A device syncs one way at a time, and only with your devices that use the same option. Photos don't sync with Cloud Sync yet; they stay on the device that added them. When Cloud Sync needs Supporter access, or WitnessWork has paused it for a while, Settings → Sync says so; your changes stay on this device and sync once it's back, and Sync now checks again. A new phone you set up from your account's QR code or recovery key gets your records through Cloud Sync without a restore step. If your newest backup is newer than every Cloud Sync copy, for example from a phone that stayed on iCloud, the new phone offers to restore it too.
faq_cloudSyncPrivacy_q: Is Cloud Sync more private than iCloud or Google Drive sync?
faq_cloudSyncPrivacy_a: Cloud Sync is always end-to-end encrypted: each device's copy is encrypted on the device with a key only your devices have, so WitnessWork's server stores data it can't read. The server sees things like your anonymous account, how many of its devices sync, and the size and time of each copy, never what's in it. iCloud and Google Drive sync store a copy in your iCloud Drive or a hidden folder of your Google Drive. Apple and Google protect it, and Apple encrypts it end to end if you turned on Advanced Data Protection, but WitnessWork doesn't encrypt iCloud or Google Drive sync end to end itself. If you lose every device and your recovery key, Cloud Sync's copies can't be read by anyone, including us.
faq_cloudSyncSwitch_q: How do I switch between Cloud Sync and iCloud or Google Drive?
faq_cloudSyncSwitch_a: Open Settings → Sync and choose Cloud Sync, iCloud (Google Drive on Android), or Off. Switching keeps everything on this device and combines it with your devices on the new option; nothing is replaced, and nothing deleted on your other devices comes back. Leaving Cloud Sync removes this device's copy from WitnessWork's server; your other devices on Cloud Sync keep what they've already synced from it. Leaving iCloud or Google Drive leaves this device's last copy there, and your other devices keep syncing with each other but not with this one. A device that already used iCloud or Google Drive before Cloud Sync keeps it, and Settings offers the switch once. To sync all your devices together, choose the same option on each.
faq_syncTroubleshooting_q: My devices are not syncing. What can I check?
faq_syncTroubleshooting_a: First check Settings → Sync: devices sync only with your devices that use the same option (Cloud Sync, iCloud, or Google Drive), so choose the same one on each. With Cloud Sync, keep the app open on both devices and check your internet connection; Sync now retries at once. If it says Cloud Sync is paused, nothing is wrong on your side: changes wait on this device and sync when it's back. For iCloud: on iOS, use the same Apple Account, turn on iCloud Drive, and enable WitnessWork under iCloud on each device. On Android, see “Google Drive Sync isn’t working on my Android device. What can I check?” iCloud sync requires Supporter access. Open Settings → iCloud Sync and use Sync now. Changes waiting to be sent are retried; an unreadable file or newer app version is shown in the status, so update every device and try again. The status shows Uploading to iCloud until Apple confirms the upload, and Last synced counts only confirmed uploads. If your iCloud storage is full, changes stay on this device; free up space or upgrade your storage in Settings → [Your Name] → iCloud and uploading resumes on its own. Keep an exported backup and the device containing your latest data. Rebuild iCloud data replaces the iCloud data with this device’s data and removes iCloud photos it doesn’t use. Your other devices switch to that data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then, and the Home bell notes it. Update WitnessWork on every device first: an older version keeps its own data until it is updated. Contact private support from the Help Center if syncing remains incomplete. Keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_syncPhotos_q: Why are contact photos missing on my other device?
faq_syncPhotos_a: Photo sync is an optional Supporter feature on iOS and Android for devices that sync with iCloud (Google Drive on Android). Open Settings → Sync and turn on Include images in sync. Photos don't sync with Cloud Sync yet; they stay on the device that added them. This uploads profile and contact photos to your private iCloud container (or WitnessWork's hidden Google Drive folder) and downloads referenced photos; they count against your iCloud or Google storage. Update WitnessWork on every device to use photo revisions safely. Pausing photo sync on one device keeps the uploaded files and local copies. To remove uploaded photos, choose Remove iCloud photos and pause photo sync on other devices first, or they can upload their copies again. Removing a contact or its photo removes downloaded copies when that change arrives; obsolete cloud copies are cleaned up after a one-day grace period. If a photo is missing, keep the device with the original, check storage and permissions, then use Sync now. Use the Help Center’s private support option if it still fails; do not include householder information in public reports.
faq_mytimeTrouble_q: MyTime Import says the file is not a database. What should I use?
faq_mytimeTrouble_a: MyTime Import needs an original .mytimedb backup created by MyTime. A PDF, text export, WitnessWork JSON backup, or a file renamed to .mytimedb will not work. To get one, go to More → Settings → Backup in MyTime and email yourself a backup, then save the attached file on your device and select it through Settings → MyTime Import. Keep the original file unchanged. If a valid backup still fails, email support privately with the error and app version; do not post the backup in a public issue.
faq_notesImportHelp_q: How does Notes Import work, and what does it cost?
faq_notesImportHelp_a: When Notes Import is available on your supported iPhone, iPad, or Android device, open it from Settings and paste readable ministry notes. On iPhone and iPad you can also record a voice log or scan your notes, and on any supported device you can choose photos of paper notes. Scribe AI proposes contacts, visits, and time entries; review the preview, assumptions, and warnings before saving selected records. If something is off, reply to Scribe AI in your own words to refine the preview; refinements don't use your allowance, and the line under Scribe AI's reply shows how many are left for those notes. The Help button explains what to include and shows the current free and Supporter allowances. Failed, cancelled, and repeated imports do not count toward the allowance. Your allowance belongs to your anonymous WitnessWork account, so Notes Import needs WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play on a device that can be verified (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). Voice logs and scans are turned into text on your device first; chosen photos are read by Scribe AI. Your notes are sent to a language-model service under a Zero Data Retention arrangement; import history stays on this device. Find the OpenRouter ZDR policy in the Notes Import Help or under Settings → About. On Android it is rolling out gradually and needs WitnessWork from Google Play; see Does Notes Import work on Android?
faq_notesImportRetry_q: Notes Import failed, is still working, or found no records. What should I do?
faq_notesImportRetry_a: Check your internet connection and follow any Update WitnessWork message. An import that stopped because the connection dropped goes on by itself when you're back online while WitnessWork is open. If an import is still working, reopen Notes Import and check its history before starting another copy. For too much text, use smaller batches; if Scribe AI cannot interpret it, add clear names, dates, and time spent, then retry. If the service is temporarily unavailable, try later. If Notes Import says it can't verify this device, see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?" If it says Notes Import has been turned off for your account, WitnessWork turned it off after a report of abuse; contact support from the Help Center if you think that's a mistake. A preview with no records means nothing was found to import. Review the preview before saving, and email support privately if the error continues.
faq_notesImportAndroid_q: Does Notes Import work on Android?
faq_notesImportAndroid_a: Yes, as it rolls out. When Notes Import appears in Settings on your Android phone or tablet, it works as it does on iPhone: paste readable notes, review what Scribe AI proposes, and save the records you choose. Voice logs and scanning aren't available on Android, so type or paste your notes, or choose photos of paper notes (see How do I bring in my paper notes?). It needs WitnessWork installed from Google Play on a Play Protect certified device, with the Google Play Store and Google Play services up to date. Notes Import uses your WitnessWork account, so Google Play Integrity checks that the app and device are genuine when this device connects to your account, and again about every 90 days (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). Google receives only that check, never your notes; your notes go only to the Scribe AI service described in How does Notes Import work. Rooted devices, custom system software, emulators, and modified or unofficial copies of the app can't be verified. If Notes Import says it can't verify this device, update the Google Play Store and Google Play services, reinstall WitnessWork from Google Play, and try again; if it still can't, Notes Import isn't supported on that device. Free and Supporter allowances are the same as on iPhone. Supporter status comes from the store you subscribed in, so an App Store subscription doesn't unlock it on Android. If Notes Import doesn't appear, update WitnessWork; it may not have reached your device yet. For anything else, use the Help Center's private support link and keep your notes out of public reports.
faq_notesImportPaper_q: How do I bring in my paper notes?
faq_notesImportPaper_a: Choose From paper in Pick up where you left off when you set up WitnessWork, or in Notes Import tap the camera and choose Choose Photos. Pick up to 10 photos of handwritten notes or record sheets, in the order you want them read. Scribe AI reads each page and puts the text in the message box, page by page. Check it, fix anything misread, and then send it to import, just like pasted notes. Reading pages doesn't use an Import Credit; sending the text is one import. If you have no Import Credits left, your pages aren't read. You can read a limited number of pages each day; if you reach it, try the rest the next day. Each photo is resized and its location and other details are removed on your device. It's then sent over an encrypted connection to Scribe AI's Zero Data Retention language-model providers, the same ones that read your notes. Neither WitnessWork nor the providers store the photo, and the app deletes its copy once the page is read or you skip it. Your original photos stay in your library. For the best results, photograph one flat, well-lit page per photo. If pages can't be read because you're offline or Scribe AI is busy, WitnessWork keeps them: tap Try Again once you're connected, without choosing the photos again, or Skip Unread Pages to keep only what was read. If a page can't be read at all, WitnessWork tells you how many were missed; type in what's missing, or try that page again with a clearer photo. If reading pages keeps failing, check your connection and try again later, or email support privately from Still need help? in the Help Center. Keep photos of your notes out of public reports. From paper needs Notes Import and an internet connection, on iPhone, iPad, and Android.
faq_notesImportVoicePhoto_q: How do voice logs and scanning work, and what leaves my device?
faq_notesImportVoicePhoto_a: In Notes Import, tap the microphone to record a voice log. For example, after a call, say who you talked with, what you discussed, and when you plan to go back. Moving bars beside the microphone show it hears you. Tap the stop button to review the text first, or tap Send to send it right away. Or tap the camera to scan handwritten notes or a house-to-house record. Speech and scanned pages are turned into text on your device, and the text appears in the message box so you can fix anything misheard or misread before you send it. Audio and scans are never saved or uploaded. Choosing photos works differently: Scribe AI reads them, as described in How do I bring in my paper notes? Only the text you send goes to Scribe AI, just like pasted notes, and each new import uses an Import Credit. A voice log stops after 10 minutes, and the microphone appears only when this device supports on-device speech recognition for your app or device language. The first recording in a language may wait while your device downloads Apple's speech model. Recording needs microphone access, plus speech recognition access before iOS 26. Scanning needs camera access. If you denied access, turn on Microphone, Speech Recognition, or Camera for WitnessWork in your device's Settings. If nothing is recognized, try again somewhere quieter or with a flat, well-lit page, or type or paste your notes instead. If it keeps failing, email support privately from Still need help? in the Help Center. Voice logs and scanning work only on iPhone and iPad; on Android, type or paste your notes, or choose photos.
faq_hourglassSetup_q: How do I send my report to Hourglass or NW Publisher?
faq_hourglassSetup_a: Open the month's Service Report, choose Hourglass or NW Publisher in the dropdown above Submit, and tap Submit. Review and send the report in the destination app. Copy and Share are also available. NW Publisher accepts only the previous month's report. Hourglass receives preaching time separately, with Credit Time included in the default report comment; if you replace the comment, check that it still says what you need. Update WitnessWork if a submission option is missing.
faq_savedContactViews_q: Can I save a contact filter and switch to it quickly?
faq_savedContactViews_a: Yes, with saved views, free on iOS and Android. In Contacts, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top, choose filters and a sort, then tap Save as view at the top and name it (up to 30 characters), such as Bible studies or Spanish territory. Your views appear as buttons under the search field, above the last-visit chips, and at the top of the map: tap one to show it, and tap it again to return to your own filters. A view applies to the list and the map alike. Search text isn't saved in a view. While a view is showing, changes you make in Sort & Filter or with the last-visit chips are marked Edited; tap Update view to keep them, Save as new view to keep both, or Reset to discard them. To reorder your views, touch one, pause briefly, then drag it along the row. Touch and hold a view without moving to rename or delete it, or choose ••• → Edit Saved Views to rename, reorder, and delete views. Deleting a view never changes your contacts. Renaming or archiving a contact field keeps views working; if you permanently delete a field, filters on it are ignored. Views are stored on your device, included in backups, and sync between your devices when sync is on; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. Which view is showing stays on each device. If a view shows unexpected contacts, open Sort & Filter to check its filters, or tap Reset to undo unsaved changes. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_contactsSuggestedSort_q: What does the Suggested sort in Contacts do?
faq_contactsSuggestedSort_a: Suggested is the Contacts list's default sort on iOS and Android. When you aren't searching, the list starts with up to four short sections: Nearby (contacts within about 250 m of you, closest first, with their street), Follow-ups Due (follow-ups due today or missed in the last 30 days, most overdue first), Recent (contacts visited in the last 2 weeks), and Been a While (people you last talked with 3 weeks to 4 months ago who have no follow-up planned, Bible studies first, then favorites, with when you last talked). A Not at Home doesn't count as talking, a follow-up missed more than 30 days ago no longer counts as planned, and a visit in the last 3 weeks, even a Not at Home, keeps someone out of Been a While. In data protection mode, Been a While stops at 90 days, when WitnessWork offers to delete old details. To take someone out of Been a While, long-press them and choose Not Now: they're dismissed for 30 days, and you can bring them back from Dismissed Contacts anytime. Each shows up to 5 contacts, and each contact appears only once. Everyone else follows under Other Contacts: favorites first, then current Bible studies, then past Bible studies, then by most recent visit. Your filters and Saved Views apply first, so the sections only include contacts the list would show. Empty sections are hidden, and if all four are empty the list is one plain list. Searching or choosing another sort also shows one plain list. Nearby is optional. It appears only if you've already allowed location for WitnessWork; the Contacts list never asks for it. It uses each contact's map pin, from their address or a pin you placed, so a contact without a location can't be Nearby. Your location is read on this device when you open Contacts, only to sort the list, and it isn't saved or sent anywhere. So rows don't move while you read, a new location shows the next time you open Contacts. To use another order, tap the Sort & Filter button (the sliders) at the top of Contacts and pick a sort; Reset returns to Suggested. If Nearby is missing, check that location is allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that the contact has a pin on the map. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names and addresses.
faq_conversationFields_q: Can I track extra details on a conversation, like the publication I used?
faq_conversationFields_a: Yes. Open Preferences → Conversation Fields, or tap Add Custom Fields on the conversation form, and add a field such as Publication. Field names can be up to 14 characters. Every field appears on the form for conversations and Not at Home visits; leave it empty when it doesn't apply. Saved values show on that visit in the contact's history. When you tap a field, values you've entered in it before appear as suggestions, most used first, and narrow as you type; tap one to fill it in. Below each field, Earlier visits lists what you entered there on that contact's previous visits, such as publications or videos you already shared, so you can choose something new. You can rename and reorder fields any time without losing what you entered. Archiving a field hides it but keeps its values. Delete it from the Archived list to remove the field and its values from every conversation for good. Fields and values stay on your device, are included in backups, and sync between your devices when sync is on; update WitnessWork on each device to see them there. They aren't included when you share a contact. Contact fields are managed separately in Preferences → Contact Fields. With data protection mode on, don't record religion, health, family situation, language, or ethnicity. If a field is missing from the form, check whether it was archived. For anything else, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_visitDetails_q: How do I see a conversation and its follow-up, or bring a buddy along?
faq_visitDetails_a: Tap a conversation in a contact's Conversation History, the Up Next card on a contact, or a person on Home's conversations card, and it opens in a sheet without leaving where you are. Tapping a follow-up reminder opens it there too. Across the top is who it was with: tap them to open the contact, or use Call, Text, and Navigate. Below, a line runs from what happened ("You talked with…", when, your note, and its fields) to the follow-up, with a Today marker in between, so you can see at a glance whether the return visit is ahead or behind. The follow-up says when you're going back and how far off it is, the topic, who's going, and the reminder. Log Visit appears once its day comes, and Reschedule while it's still open. A missed follow-up turns amber, one you kept links to the visit that kept it, and a dismissed one can be planned again. With no follow-up, the sheet links to your next visit with that person, or offers Plan the next visit after the latest one. Tap the pencil to edit, or ••• to reschedule, copy the note or topic, dismiss the follow-up, or delete the conversation; deleting can't be undone. If you use Buddies, invited buddies and their answers show inside the follow-up. While it's still ahead, the dashed + invites someone right away and shares only its date and time, the householder's first name, the address, and the topic. To take someone off, edit the conversation. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. Opening a conversation changes nothing, and only inviting a buddy shares anything. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_followUpReminders_q: Can I keep visit notes without scheduling a return visit or reminder?
faq_followUpReminders_a: Yes. When adding or editing a visit, turn off Follow Up and save. The visit and its notes remain, but that visit has no scheduled follow-up or reminder and will not appear as overdue. You can turn Follow Up on later and choose a date and time. To stop an older follow-up reminder, edit that visit and turn Follow Up off.
faq_followUpCard_q: How do I use the Today's Conversations card on Home?
faq_followUpCard_a: The card shows the follow-ups you scheduled for today. From 5 PM it shows Upcoming Conversations, which adds tomorrow's; those can be rescheduled but not logged until their day. Swipe sideways to move between people. When you've been, tap Talked to log the conversation in the visit form, or tap Not at Home to log the attempt right away. Undo appears below the card for a few seconds after Not at Home. The calendar button reschedules the follow-up. Tap a person to see that conversation and its follow-up in a sheet. Use the ••• button or touch and hold a person for call, message, directions, Open Contact, and Dismiss Follow-Up. A follow-up counts as done once you log any visit with that person on or after its day. The bar at the top fills as you go, and the card shows All caught up when every one is done. Tap Done, or touch and hold the title and choose Close for Now, to hide the card until you add or reschedule a follow-up. A follow-up still open 4 hours after its time moves to missed follow-ups in the notifications tray. Not at Home is unavailable while data protection mode is on. Visits are saved like any other visit on this device. To remove the card for good, touch and hold its title, choose Edit Home Screen, and tap the minus on the card. Add Sections brings it back while you edit Home. If something looks wrong, contact support from the Help Center and leave out names, addresses, and notes.
faq_logVisit_q: How do I quickly log a visit?
faq_logVisit_a: Tap + and choose Log Visit, then pick the person. On iPad, Log Visit… is also in the menu bar's File menu. Without searching, the list starts with Nearby (contacts within about 250 m of you, closest first), then Follow-ups Due (today's and missed ones from the last 30 days), then Recent (visited in the last 2 weeks), then All Contacts A–Z. Type to search; if the person isn't there, tap Add as a new contact to create them and log the visit next. After you pick someone, tap Had a Conversation to add notes and a follow-up in the visit form, or Not at Home to log it right away, with Undo at the bottom of the screen for a few seconds. On a contact's page, + Add → Not at Home logs it the same way. In data protection mode, Not at Home isn't offered and the visit form opens directly. Nearby is optional: it appears only if you allow location, and you're never asked unless you tap Turn On. Your location is used on this device only to sort the list; it isn't saved or sent anywhere. If Nearby is missing, check that location is allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings and that the contact has a location on the map. Touch and hold a person to open their contact instead.
faq_reminders_q: How do follow-up, plan, and contact reminders work?
faq_reminders_a: Turn on Notify Me when adding or editing a Follow-up or a Plan, then choose how long before it starts the reminder should arrive. A recurring Plan reminds you the same amount of time before each of its dates, counting from that date's own start time if you changed it for that date only. Dates you deleted, and dates after its end date, don't remind you. Each device schedules a recurring Plan's reminders up to two weeks ahead, so open WitnessWork at least every two weeks to keep them coming. Dismissing a contact also reminds you when they're available again. If Notify Me is off because notifications aren't allowed, turning it on asks for permission; if you've declined before, it opens your device settings. If a one-time Plan's or Follow-up's reminder time has already passed, the form says so and no reminder is sent. Rescheduling keeps the reminder time you chose. When a reminder arrives, it is also listed in the Home bell, even if system notifications are off, and tapping either one opens the follow-up, plan, or contact. Each device schedules its own reminders from your saved records, so after a sync or a backup restore, open WitnessWork once on that device to set them up. Deleting a visit, plan, or contact removes its reminders, including any already shown. With data protection mode on, reminders leave out names and topics. On Android, the system may deliver a reminder a few minutes late to save battery. If reminders don't arrive, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in Preferences and in your device settings, and that Focus or Do Not Disturb isn't silencing them. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_appIconBadge_q: Why is there a number on the WitnessWork app icon?
faq_appIconBadge_a: On iOS, the number on the app icon is how many items in the Home notification bell you haven't read yet. News from your buddies, like a buddy's new badge or a reaction to yours, is never counted. Open the bell and scroll through it to mark items read; dismissing or clearing them also lowers the number. It updates while WitnessWork is open and when a Follow-up, Plan, or contact reminder arrives. Other items, like last month's report or a buddy's invitation, are counted the next time you open WitnessWork, so the number can be behind while the app is closed. Each device keeps its own count. The number needs notification permission; to hide it, turn off Badges for WitnessWork in your device's notification settings. That setting only affects this number, not the badges you grow on your profile. On Android, the app icon doesn't show an unread count; your launcher may show a dot for notifications in the notification shade. If the number looks wrong, open WitnessWork, then leave it to refresh the count. If it still doesn't match the bell, contact support from the Help Center.
faq_soundEffects_q: How do I turn off celebration and reminder sounds?
faq_soundEffects_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Play sounds. This controls celebration chimes and reminders while WitnessWork is open; reminders still appear, just without sound (on Android, as a short message in the app). Reminders received while the app is closed follow your device's notification settings; adjust those separately if needed.
faq_haptics_q: How do I turn off vibrations?
faq_haptics_a: Open Settings → Preferences → Audio & Haptics and turn off Haptics. WitnessWork then stops all of its vibration feedback, such as taps, chart scrubbing, and goal celebrations. The setting applies only to this device and isn't synced to your other devices. Some system controls, like menus and switches, may still vibrate based on your device's own settings; adjust those in your device's sound and haptics settings.
faq_routePlanning_q: How do I plan a route for my service day?
faq_routePlanning_a: Route planning is a Supporter feature on iPhone, iPad, and Android. Open it from any day from today on: tap the day on Home or in Schedule (on iPad, the day's details show beside the calendar), then tap Plan Route; or touch and hold a day and choose Plan Route; or choose Plan Route in a plan's menu to plan the day around that plan. On Home, Plan Route also shows at the top of the conversations card when at least two of today's stops have a map location. A day with no follow-ups or plans can still be planned from scratch. Anyone can open it to see the day on the map; Shortest Order and Start Route need Supporter. The map shows your route with a card at each stop saying when you'd get there, and the box at the top shows when the day starts, when it finishes, and how long that is. Zoom in to see cards that would overlap, and drag the bar under the map to make it taller or shorter. On iPad and other wide screens the map sits beside the list. Use the arrows beside the date to plan another day. Stops start as the day's open follow-ups and plans that have an address or pin. Follow-ups already answered by a visit that day, and follow-ups for dismissed contacts, aren't included. Tap Add Stop to add Home, your Kingdom Hall, a place or address from search (you can also paste coordinates such as 37.7749, -122.4194 or a map link there), one of your contacts, or a pin you drop on the Map tab. You can also touch and hold the route map to drop a pin and add it as a stop, the start, or the finish. A route can have up to 10 stops. To change the order, drag a stop by its grip, or touch and hold it and drag; you can also use Move Up and Move Down in the stop's ⋯ menu. Shortest Order asks the WitnessWork server for the fastest driving order; it needs an internet connection, works with up to 10 stops, and can be used 10 times in any 24 hours. Remove a stop from its menu; the day's stops you remove are listed below so you can add them back. Set how long you'll spend at each stop with its time chip. Between stops, the line shows the drive and, when you'd get somewhere early, how long you'd wait. Times are estimates from the distance between stops, so check them against fixed appointments. A stop shows when you'd be late for its set time. With Start Visits at Set Times on (in Details, when a stop has a set time), arriving early waits until the set time; turn it off to see how early you'd get there. In Details, link the route to one of the day's plans, invite buddies, and add notes with formatting, lists, and links. Your route is saved on this device for that day and isn't synced to your other devices. Tap Start Over to rebuild it from the day's follow-ups and plans. Planning a route never changes your contacts, follow-ups, or plans. For other problems, use the Help Center's private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.
faq_routePlanningPlaces_q: How do I choose where my route starts and finishes, or save Home and my Kingdom Hall?
faq_routePlanningPlaces_a: At the top of the route, tap the place under Start to choose your current location, the first stop, Home, your Kingdom Hall, one of the day's plans that has a place, or any place you search for, and tap the time to change when you leave. If a plan with a place starts before your first follow-up, such as a meeting for field service, the route starts there at that time. At the bottom, tap the place under Finish to end at the last stop (the default), go back to where you started, or finish at Home, your Kingdom Hall, or any place you search for. The finish isn't a stop, so there's no time spent there; the drive to it is added, and the finish time is when you'd get there. Start Route takes your navigation app on to the finish. Shortest Order puts the stops in order from the start and keeps the finish last. To save Home or your Kingdom Hall, tap Set Home or Set Kingdom Hall in the Start or Finish menu, or in Add Stop, then search for the address or drop a pin on the Map tab. After that, they're one tap away in those menus and in Add Stop. To change or remove one, touch and hold it in Add Stop. Saved places stay on this device and aren't synced.
faq_routePlanningBuddies_q: How do I plan a route with buddies?
faq_routePlanningBuddies_a: Invitations go out with a plan, so a route's buddies are its plan's buddies. In the route's Details, tap Invite Buddies. If the route already belongs to one of the day's one-time plans, the row opens to your buddies: tap one to invite them to that plan right away, and tap them again to take them off, which cancels their invitation. If the route doesn't have a plan yet, Invite Buddies opens a new plan filled in from the route's day, start time, and starting place; choose who to invite there and save, and the route then belongs to that plan. Buddies get the plan's date, time, title, location, and note, plus any changes you make to the plan, and they can say whether they're going; their answers show in Details. They don't get the route's stops, order, or notes. You can also start from the plan: choose Plan Route in its menu to plan the day around it. Plans that follow a buddy's invitation are invited to by their organizer, and recurring plans can't carry invitations, so Invite Buddies doesn't show for them. Buddies must be set up first: with no buddies yet, Invite Buddies opens Buddies.
faq_routePlanningNavigation_q: How does my route open in Apple Maps, Google Maps, or Waze?
faq_routePlanningNavigation_a: Tap Start Route. Your route opens in the Default Navigation App chosen in Settings → Preferences → Navigation, in the order shown, starting with the place you chose as the start when it isn't your current location, and ending where you chose to finish when that isn't the last stop. Google Maps opens the whole route as one trip with every stop in order. Apple Maps does the same on iOS 18.4 or later; on earlier versions it opens one stop at a time. Waze always opens one stop at a time because its links accept only a single destination. When stops open one at a time, come back to WitnessWork and tap Navigate to Stop 2 (and so on) for the next stop. To go to any one stop, open its menu and tap Navigate Here. If Google Maps isn't installed, the route opens in a web browser, which may show fewer stops; install the app or choose another navigation app. On Android, choose Google Maps or Waze. If a map app doesn't open, check that it's installed and try again.
faq_routePlanningPrivacy_q: What's shared when I plan a route?
faq_routePlanningPrivacy_a: To find the order, WitnessWork sends the map coordinates of your starting point and each stop to the WitnessWork server, which passes only those coordinates to HERE, a mapping service, to calculate the drive. Names, addresses, notes, topics, and visit details are never sent. The request also carries the app's random account identifier, the one tied to your Supporter purchase, so the server can confirm Supporter status and count your routes; it isn't sent to HERE. The server doesn't store coordinates. It keeps only the times of your route requests from the last 24 hours to apply the daily limit. When you open the route, your navigation app receives each stop's address, or its coordinates for a pin you placed, and the place you finish when it isn't the last stop, just as it does when you navigate to a single contact. Usage analytics record counts such as how many stops a route had, never locations. The route you build, including its notes, added stops, and where it starts and finishes, is saved only on this device; it isn't sent anywhere or synced. So are the addresses you save as Home and Kingdom Hall. Buddies you invite get the route's plan, the same as inviting them from the plan: its date, time, title, location, and note. They don't get the route, its stops, or its notes.
faq_locationTrouble_q: Why can't the map find my current location?
faq_locationTrouble_a: Check that location services are on and WitnessWork has location permission in your device's settings. Reopen the map and try again where your device can obtain a location. You can still enter an address or place a contact's pin manually without using your current location. If the problem continues, report the error with your device and operating-system version, leaving private contact details out of screenshots.
faq_mapFilters_q: Why are some contacts missing from the map?
faq_mapFilters_a: The map shows your active contacts that have an address or a pin, and it uses the same filters as your Contacts list. Last-visit chips, Saved Views, and filters from Sort & Filter all apply to both, so a contact hidden from the list is hidden from the map too. The chips at the top of the map show what's on; tap All, tap the selected Saved View again, or open Sort & Filter (the sliders at the top) and tap Reset to see everyone. If the chips are tucked away after you move the map, tap the Contacts title to bring them back. The map's own search only narrows the pins further and doesn't change the list. A contact you create by dropping a pin stays on the map until you switch to the list, even if your filters would hide it. Dismissed contacts don't appear; find them under ••• → Dismissed Contacts. A contact without an address or pin can't appear either; open the contact and add an address or place its pin. A contact with an address but no pin yet, such as one from an import, appears once its address is looked up: when the map has any, tap Find contacts on the map at the top to look them all up, or tap X to hide it. This sends those addresses to the WitnessWork server, which looks them up with HERE, a mapping service, and doesn't keep them. An address that can't be found isn't offered again until you edit it; place that contact's pin by hand instead. In data protection mode, addresses are never looked up, so place pins by hand. A contact saved without an internet connection appears once you're back online with WitnessWork open; if it still doesn't, edit its address or place its pin. This works the same on iOS and Android, and filters are worked out on your device; they aren't shared. If a contact is still missing, check its address, then contact support from the Help Center and leave out names and addresses.
faq_restoreSupporter_q: I already paid, but Supporter features or prices are missing. What should I do?
faq_restoreSupporter_a: Check your connection and that your device's store uses the account you purchased with. Open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases when it is shown. A one-time Tip does not activate Supporter features. If no purchases are found, prices do not load, or your subscription still is not recognized, email support privately with your app version and what happened. If support needs your account ID, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help?, then tap Copy Account ID. Share that ID privately. Restoring purchases restores access, not your service records.
faq_foundingSupporter_a: Founding Supporters were already supporting WitnessWork before the Supporter tier launched in May 2026, when support came with no perks at all. The label is simply our thank-you. It isn't a separate tier: Founding Supporters get the same features as every other Supporter, and it can't be purchased or earned now. While your support is active, Founding Supporter appears on your profile and in Settings. It comes from your Supporter start date, so nothing extra is stored or shared. If your support lapses, the label is hidden until you support again. It returns if your store account still reports your original start date, which is usually the case when you resubscribe with the same account. If you expected to see it, open Settings → Become a supporter and use Restore Purchases. If it still doesn't appear, use the support button in this screen's header to open Still need help? and contact support privately.
faq_buddiesOverview_q: What is WitnessWork Buddies, and why don't I see it?
faq_buddiesOverview_a: Buddies lets you connect with up to five people you go out in service with and see each other's planned days, start times, and durations for the next eight weeks. You also see the badges each buddy shares. It works on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and buddies on different platforms can connect with each other. On the Schedule calendar, a buddy's photo or initial on a day means you're going out together, and a small dot under a day means other buddies plan to go out. Tap the day to see who. On iPhone and iPad, the Calendar widget shows the same marks and updates when WitnessWork refreshes Buddies, so open the app if it looks behind.
