It is free when available, and needs WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play on a device that can be verified (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). Open Schedule, tap Buddies at the top, and complete the introduction with your profile name. A dot on that button means a request is waiting for you to confirm. Buddies may be unavailable during rollout. Update the installed app if the Buddies button is missing. If the button is dimmed, Buddies is temporarily unavailable; your saved buddies stay on your calendar, so try again later.
faq_buddiesAdd_q: How do I add a buddy, and who confirms the request?
faq_buddiesAdd_a: Open Buddies from Schedule, or tap Invite Buddies on a new Plan before you have a buddy, and tap Invite a Buddy or the + button to share a Buddies Invite. To pair in person, use the code button to show your Buddies Code and have the other person scan it inside WitnessWork. You can also paste a link through Enter Invite Link. The recipient taps Accept; the person who created the invite then opens Buddies → Requests and taps Confirm. You start seeing each other's plans only after that confirmation. Confirm only the person you intended to invite.
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_q: Why is my Buddies Invite waiting, expired, or saying all spots are in use?
faq_buddiesInviteTrouble_a: An accepted request waits until the inviter confirms it in Buddies → Requests. Each Buddies Invite works once and expires after seven days; ask for a new link if it was used, cancelled, or expired. Your five spots include buddies and pending invites or requests. Cancel an unused invite or remove a buddy to make room. Only a limited number of unused invite links can be open at once. If tapping an invite link opens a web page instead of WitnessWork, install WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play and tap the link again, or copy the link and paste it in Buddies → Enter Invite Link. If scanning is unavailable, allow camera access in your device's settings or share and paste the invite link instead.
faq_buddiesPrivacy_q: What can my buddies see, and is sharing private?
faq_buddiesPrivacy_a: Buddies always see your name and the days you plan to go out over the next eight weeks, with how long you plan. Your photo (which buddies can tap to see full size), pioneer status, streak, badges, pet (its kind, coat, and name), and your Plans' start times are shared unless you turn them off in Buddies Settings. Badges go without progress, counts, or dates. Under Your Plans, Start times can share the exact time, only the time of day (Morning, Afternoon, or Evening), or no time at all, and Pause sharing hides your plans, streak, badges, and pet from every buddy for a week, a month, or until you turn it back on. Each of these can be different for one buddy: open their page and tap Sharing & Alerts. Buddies aren't told when you change any of this. Calendar sharing never includes your recorded service time, reports, goals, categories, contact list, visit history, or notes. Shared content is end-to-end encrypted so only you and the buddies you choose can read it. WitnessWork's server knows you only by an anonymous account number your device made, never your name, email, or phone number. Explicit Plan and Follow-up invitations share extra details, including a Plan's note (and its photos) or a Follow-up's address; check those details before inviting someone. Find the Privacy Policy under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header.
faq_buddiesPause_q: Can I pause sharing or hide when I go out?
faq_buddiesPause_a: Yes. Open Buddies, tap the menu button, and choose Buddies Settings. Under Your Plans, Start times sets how precisely buddies see when you go out: Exact time, Time of day (Morning before noon, Afternoon until 5 PM, Evening after that), or Don't share. Buddies still see which days you plan and for how long. Pause sharing hides your plans, streak, badges, and pet from every buddy for a week, a month, or until you turn it back on; they still see your name and photo, and new badges aren't announced. While a pause is on, Buddies shows Sharing is paused with a Resume button. A timed pause ends by itself, and your plans return to buddies the next time WitnessWork refreshes Buddies on your device. To stop sharing plans with just one buddy, open their page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Share my plans; a pause still covers them too. Buddies aren't told about any of these choices, though they may notice your plans are gone. Plan and Follow-up invitations you send still go out while sharing is paused. Your choices apply on all your devices with Buddies. Your photo, pioneer status, streak, badges, and pet each have their own switch under How buddies see you.
faq_buddiesPerBuddy_q: Can I share different things with different buddies?
faq_buddiesPerBuddy_a: Yes. Buddies Settings starts with All Buddies: the settings every buddy follows. To change any of them for one buddy, tap Choose a buddy at the top of Buddies Settings (All Buddies / Choose a buddy) and pick them, or open their page and tap Sharing & Alerts. You can choose, just for them, your photo, pioneer status, streak, badges, pet, whether they see your plans and how precisely start times show, whether their plans show on your calendar, and Ask to Join Alerts and Badge Alerts on this device. A setting that's theirs alone has a highlighted layers icon and an undo arrow beside its name: tap the undo arrow to have them follow All Buddies again, or the undo arrow at the top to do that for all of their settings. Tap the layers icon to see their value and All Buddies', with a checkmark on the one in use. In All Buddies, a setting some buddies have their own value for has a layers icon that lists them; tap a buddy there to open their settings. Tap All Buddies at the top to go back. Undo in the top corner takes back your changes on that screen, newest first. Changing an All Buddies setting changes it for every buddy who follows it, but not for a buddy with their own. Pause sharing is for everyone: while it's on, no buddy sees your plans, streak, badges, or pet, whatever their own settings. Your name always goes to every buddy, and buddies aren't told about any of these choices. Sharing and calendar settings apply on all your devices with Buddies; alerts apply only to the device you set them on.
faq_buddiesAskToJoin_q: How do I ask to join a buddy's Plan?
faq_buddiesAskToJoin_a: Tap a day on your Schedule calendar, then tap Ask to Join next to a buddy who plans to go out that day. You can also tap one of their days under Next two weeks on their details screen. Your request shares only what you already see: the day, time, and length of their Plan. It shows as Asked until your buddy invites you, you withdraw it, or the Plan starts; tap Asked to withdraw it. Asking closes two hours before the Plan starts, and you can have up to three requests waiting with each buddy. Your buddy is alerted only the first time you ask for a Plan, and for at most three requests a day. If they move or remove that Plan, your request is withdrawn for you. Asked shows only on the device you asked from. When your buddy invites you, answer in the notification bell on Home. If you choose Going while you already have your own Plan at that time, one-time or recurring, you can replace it for that day so your time isn't counted twice. A recurring plan keeps going on your other days.
faq_buddiesJoinRequests_q: How do I answer or turn off requests to join my Plans?
faq_buddiesJoinRequests_a: When a buddy asks to join one of your Plans, their request appears in the notification bell on Home. Tap Invite to add them to your Plan and send the invitation right away; the button turns into a check. Tap the request itself to open the Plan, where Invite works the same way. Tap Not Now (or dismiss it) to clear it quietly: your buddy is never told, and the request lapses when the Plan starts. If the Plan came from someone else's invitation, only its organizer can invite. Inviting someone to one date of a recurring plan turns that date into its own one-time Plan, and the recurring plan stays the same on your other days. If your Plans that day changed since they asked, open the Plan you're keeping to invite them. To stop alerts for every request, turn off Ask to Join Alerts in Buddies Settings. To stop alerts from one buddy, open their page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Ask to Join Alerts, or long-press their request and choose Turn Off Alerts. With alerts off for everyone, you can turn them on there for one buddy. Requests still appear in the bell either way. Not Now and these settings apply to this device only, so a request you cleared on one device can still show on another.
faq_buddiesInvitations_q: How do I invite a buddy to a Plan or Follow-up, and answer an invitation?
faq_buddiesInvitations_a: Use Invite Buddies when adding or editing a Plan or scheduled Follow-up, select confirmed buddies, and save. On a Plan's page, or a conversation's page for a scheduled Follow-up, Invite Buddies invites someone right away. You can also tap Invite to a Plan on a buddy's page. A Plan invite shares its date, time, duration, title, location, and note, with the note's formatting and photos. A Follow-up invite shares its date/time, the householder's first name, address or pin, and topic; those details expire a day after the visit. Check that you want to share these details with the people selected. Follow-up invitations are unavailable in Data Protection Mode. To reply, choose Going or Can't Make It in the notification bell on Home, on the buddy's page in Buddies, or on the invitation's own page (tap it in the bell, on the buddy's page, or on the day in Schedule to open it); you can change your answer later. A Follow-up invitation's page shows when your buddy is going, the householder's first name, the topic, and the place, with directions. An invitation stays in the bell until you answer it, it is canceled, or its Plan or Follow-up has happened, so it can't be dismissed or cleared by mistake; once answered, you can dismiss it. Going to a Plan adds a linked Plan to your schedule, which follows the inviter's changes or cancellation until the Plan happens; after that it stays on your schedule as it was. A buddy's shared Plan stays open to you for a month after it. Can't Make It takes it off your schedule, and switching back to Going on the Plan's page puts it back. If someone stops being your buddy before an invitation reaches them, WitnessWork tells you, and the Plan shows Not sent beside them until it has happened. A Follow-up invite does not import the contact or visit history.
faq_buddiesNotifications_q: What do Buddies notifications say, and who can see them?
faq_buddiesNotifications_a: Buddies notifications say who did what, using the nickname you gave that buddy if you set one: for example, “Anna invited you to a Plan” with its day and time, “Joe can't make it,” “Levi would like to join you,” or “Levi earned a badge” with the badge's name. A Follow-up notification shows only its day and time, never the householder's name, address, or topic, and a Plan notification never shows its title, place, or note. WitnessWork's server never sees these names or details: each notification arrives with your buddy's message still encrypted, and your device opens it and writes the notification itself. Right after your device restarts, before you first unlock it, or when the message can't be read, you get a general notification such as “New invitation” instead; open the notification bell on Home to see who it's from. If notifications never name anyone, update WitnessWork. Notifications can show on your lock screen; to hide what they say until you unlock, change the lock screen settings in your device's notification settings. To choose which Buddies notifications this device gets, use Buddies notifications, Ask to Join Alerts, and Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings, or change them for one buddy under Sharing & Alerts on their page. Everything still appears in the notification bell, and what you read or clear there is read or cleared on your other devices with Buddies too. On Android, Buddies notifications need Google Play services. If they stop arriving, check that notifications are allowed for WitnessWork in your device settings, then open Buddies to refresh. If they still don't arrive, report the problem from the Help Center without including names or other private details.
faq_buddiesDetail_q: What's on a buddy's page, and can I rename them or change their color?
faq_buddiesDetail_a: Open Buddies and tap a buddy; tap their photo to see it full size. Needs your answer lists their invitations you haven't answered; choose Going or Can't Make It there or in the Home notification bell. Together lists upcoming Plans and Follow-ups between you two, whoever invited whom, with each answer; tap a Plan to open its page, or use the menu on a buddy's invitation to change your answer. Next two weeks shows the days your buddy plans to go out next to your own; tap one of their days to plan the same time or ask to join. Invite to a Plan opens a new Plan with that buddy already invited, and View on Calendar opens Schedule. A nickname is a private name only you see; your buddy isn't told, and clearing it brings back their own name. Supporters can choose a buddy's color from the same swatches as the accent color, or any color with the eyedropper; Default brings back the color given when you paired, which everyone else keeps. Nicknames and colors are kept with your encrypted Buddies data, so they return when Buddies restores on another device. Nickname and color are right under their card, so you see a change as you make it. Sharing & Alerts opens their settings: what they see, whether their plans show on your calendar, and alerts. Their full schedule for the next eight weeks is on your calendar while Show on my calendar is on.
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_q: Why are a buddy's plans or invitations missing or out of date?
faq_buddiesMissingPlans_a: Check that the request has been confirmed and Show on my calendar is on for that buddy. Your buddy may have paused sharing, or stopped sharing plans with you; WitnessWork doesn't say when they do. A buddy who shares only the time of day or no start time shows Morning, Afternoon, Evening, or Planned in place of a time. Calendar sharing covers only the next eight weeks. Both people need an internet connection to send and receive changes; open Buddies and pull down to refresh. Previously downloaded plans remain viewable offline, but new changes need a connection; Buddies says when you're offline, when it couldn't refresh, or when it can't verify this device. Seeing a buddy's calendar does not add their plans to yours. Turn on Buddies notifications in Buddies Settings and your device's notification settings, and check the Home notification bell for invitations even if no notification arrived. On Android, Buddies notifications need Google Play services; without them, changes still arrive when you open WitnessWork. The bell checks for new Buddies activity when you open it and when you return to WitnessWork; if it says it couldn't check, reconnect and tap Try Again.
faq_buddiesNotSent_q: Why does my answer say Sending in or Not sent yet, or my request say Waiting to Send?
faq_buddiesNotSent_a: Going is sent to your buddy right away. Can't Make It waits 15 seconds first, in case you tapped it by mistake: tap Change to fix it before it's sent. Leaving the app sends it right away. Not sent yet or Waiting to Send means your answer or Ask to Join request hasn't reached your buddy, usually because you're offline or Buddies is temporarily unavailable. You don't need to answer or ask again: it's saved on this device and sends automatically the next time Buddies refreshes, such as when you open Buddies or return to WitnessWork while connected. While WitnessWork is open, it tries once more on its own shortly after. To send it sooner, reconnect and tap Try Again beside Your answer on the Plan or Follow-up, or open Buddies and pull down to refresh. Your buddy won't see the answer or request until it's sent.
faq_buddiesRemove_q: How do I hide a buddy, stop sharing, or delete my Buddies data?
faq_buddiesRemove_a: Open a buddy's page, tap Sharing & Alerts, and turn off Show on my calendar to hide their plans on your calendar on all your devices with Buddies; sharing continues, and your own Plans with them still show. Remove Buddy ends the connection for both people, and reconnecting takes a new invite. They are not notified, though they may notice. If removal is pending while offline, they may still see your last shared plans until WitnessWork reconnects and completes it. Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data removes all connections and invites and erases your encrypted Buddies data and encryption identity. It cannot be undone; reconnect and retry if deletion is pending. Your personal service records and contacts remain.
faq_buddiesSuspended_q: Why does Buddies say it's been turned off for me?
faq_buddiesSuspended_a: WitnessWork can turn off Buddies for someone after a report of abuse, such as harassing a buddy. While it's off, Buddies can't sync, send invites, or share Plans. A Plan or Follow-up you invite buddies to then isn't sent, now or later: the app tells you, and the Plan shows Not sent beside them (change it once Buddies is back on to send it). You can still remove buddies and delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data). Your buddies aren't notified. WitnessWork knows you only by an anonymous account number your device made, with no name, email, or phone number, and can't read anything you share with buddies. If you think this is a mistake, contact support under Still need help?, using the support button in this screen's header, and include your app version. If the report was wrong, we turn Buddies back on.
faq_buddiesRestore_q: Can I recover my buddies on another device or from a backup?
faq_buddiesRestore_a: On iPhone and iPad, your Buddies encryption key is kept in iCloud Keychain, so your buddies follow you to your other devices signed in to the same Apple Account with iCloud Keychain on (Passwords, in iCloud settings), and come back after you reinstall WitnessWork. With sync on, Buddies starts by itself on your other devices once they sync: your buddies, your answers to invitations, the notifications you've read or cleared, and the nicknames and colors you chose show on each one, and each device gets Buddies notifications (choose which in Buddies Settings on that device). Without sync, open Buddies on the other device and pull down to refresh. Each device then shares the plans it has, so turn on sync to keep what your buddies see the same. Your buddies see one name for you from all your devices: the one you last changed in Profile on a device using Buddies. Buddies Settings shows it under How buddies see you. On Android, Google Play services keeps the key: it comes back when you reinstall WitnessWork on the same phone while Google backup is on (Settings → Google → Backup), and with a screen lock set it's also saved, end-to-end encrypted, in your Google backup, so it can return when you set up a new phone from that backup. Without a screen lock, the key stays on that phone. Android devices don't share one key the way iCloud Keychain does, so each Android device, and an iPhone and an Android phone, have their own Buddies connections. Regular WitnessWork backup files do not contain the encryption key. If the key is unavailable, or you used Delete My Buddies Data, reconnect with new invites. A device whose key went missing can still delete the Buddies data it kept, or sign in to another account; buddies of the old key keep that connection until they remove it. Keep your personal records backed up separately.
faq_mileageStart_a: Mileage Tracking is optional and available for every publisher type. Answer Yes on the "Track mileage?" card on Home, or turn on Track Mileage in Settings → Profile. Then add your first car; only a name is required. Log a trip with Log Trip on Home's Mileage card, from the Add button, or on the Mileage screen. Enter the distance (turn on Round Trip to double it) or switch to Odometer and enter start and end readings. Odometer Start fills in from that car's last reading. Tap a trip to see its details, or long-press it to edit, log it again today, share, or delete it.
faq_mileageCost_q: How is the estimated fuel cost calculated, and what happens when fuel prices change?
faq_mileageCost_a: Estimated fuel cost is distance ÷ the car's fuel economy × its fuel's price, using the values in effect on each trip's date. It only appears once the car has a fuel economy and its fuel has a price; trips without both are left out and the report says so. A fuel's price is shared by every car that uses that fuel. When you change a price or a car's fuel economy, choose From a Date to apply it from that day forward (earlier trips keep the old value) or Fix Current Value to correct a mistake, which also updates the past trips that used it. Each fuel and car keeps a history; long-press an entry to delete it. The amount is only an estimate. If you're reimbursed, the actual amount is calculated by whoever reimburses you.
faq_mileageUnits_q: Can I use kilometers, litres, or L/100 km?
faq_mileageUnits_a: Yes. Open Mileage → Settings (the gear) → Units. Distance can be miles or kilometers, and fuel economy can be mpg (US), mpg (UK), L/100 km, or km/L. Auto follows your device's region. Fuel is priced per gallon with mpg (US) and per litre with every other choice. Currency follows your device's region. Changing units only changes how numbers are shown; your trips aren't altered.
faq_mileageShare_q: How do I share or export my mileage report?
faq_mileageShare_a: Open Mileage, choose Day, Week, Month, or Year (service year, September to August), and use the arrows or swipe to pick the period. Tap the share button at the top to Copy the report, Share it as text, or Export CSV for a spreadsheet. The text lists totals, per-car totals when you have more than one car, and each trip except in the Year view. The CSV has one row per trip with the car, odometer readings, distance, note, fuel, fuel economy, price, and estimated cost. Trip notes are included, so check them before sending. To share one trip, open it and tap the share button.
faq_mileageCars_q: What's the difference between archiving and deleting a car?
faq_mileageCars_a: Open Mileage → Settings, tap the car, and choose Archive or Delete…. Archiving hides the car from new trips but keeps its trips in your reports; unarchive it anytime from Archived Cars. Deleting removes the car and all of its trips on every device that syncs with this one, and can't be undone. Deleting a fuel removes its price history, so cars using it stop showing an estimated cost.
faq_mileageSync_q: Does my mileage sync, and does it work on Android?
faq_mileageSync_a: Mileage works on iOS and Android. Cars, fuels, prices, and trips sync between your devices with Device Sync, a Supporter feature, using the option you choose in Settings → Sync: Cloud Sync, which also syncs between iPhone and Android, or iCloud (Google Drive on Android). They're included in WitnessWork Backup (Settings → Account) and in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore on both platforms. Mileage is never shared with Buddies and doesn't appear on your calendar or Service Report.
faq_mileageTurnOff_q: How do I turn mileage tracking on or off?
faq_mileageChart_q: What does the chart on the Mileage screen show?
faq_mileageChart_a: Open the Mileage screen and choose Week, Month, or Year. The chart shows how far you drove each day, or each month of the service year (September through August). When more than one car has trips in that period, each bar is split by car, using the colors next to each car's total. Tap a bar to open that day or month and see its trips. The Day view has no chart, and a period without trips shows none. Bars show distance, not estimated cost.
faq_mileageTurnOff_a: Use the Track Mileage switch in Settings → Profile. Turning it off hides the Home card, the Log Trip action, and the Mileage screen, but keeps your trips; turn it back on and everything returns. If you chose No Thanks on the Home card, this switch turns it on anytime. To erase your mileage, open Mileage → Settings → Delete All Mileage Data. This deletes it on every device that syncs with this one and can't be undone. You can also hide only the Home card with Settings → Preferences → Home Screen.
faq_petStart_q: How do I get a pet, and how do I turn it off?
faq_petStart_a: The Pet Companion is optional and works on iOS and Android. On Home, the Meet your companion card offers one: tap Choose a pet, pick a lion cub, pup, kitten, donkey, or lamb (the pup and the kitten come in several coats), give it a name if you like, and tap Adopt. A short intro then shows how its hearts fill, how your streak opens up hats and room items, and how to decorate; tap Next through it, or close it to skip it. If you chose Not now, bring the offer back with Add Sections while editing Home (press and hold an empty space on Home), or turn on Pet in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. To hide the pet, long-press its card, choose Edit Home Screen, and tap the gray minus on it, or turn off Pet in Settings → Preferences → Home Screen. Hiding keeps your pet, its room, and its keepsakes; turn Pet back on and everything returns. You have one companion at a time.
faq_petHearts_q: How do my pet’s hearts work?
faq_petHearts_a: A new pet starts with 3 of 5 hearts, or 4 if you were active the day before you adopted it. Each day you're active in the ministry adds one heart, up to 5. A day counts when you log time (including marking that you shared in the ministry, even with 0 minutes), save a visit (a conversation, return visit, or not-at-home), or make a new plan (editing a plan doesn't count). Visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs, so they don't count. One heart a day, however much you did; hours don't matter. When 10 days pass without an active day, your pet loses half a heart every 3 days. At half a heart it falls asleep, and after 60 days without an active day it dies (it's shown greyed and lying down). Kingdom Publishers go by the month instead, as they report: an active day fills all 5 hearts (a pet adopted in a month you've already been active starts with all 5), and they stay full through the next month, so marking once a month that you shared keeps your pet happy. If a whole month passes without an active day, its hearts start fading 10 days into the month after, as above, and an active day fills them right back up. Tap a sleeping pet (or, if it died, Tap to wake) to wake it with 1 heart; the next active day adds hearts again. Patting it (tap it, or drag across it to rub) is just for fun and never adds hearts. Hearts are worked out from your records each time, so they're the same on every device and come back if you restore a backup.
faq_petLamp_q: What does the lamp in the room mean?
faq_petLamp_a: The lamp is your Service Streak. It burns brighter as your streak grows, from unlit at 0 to its brightest once your streak reaches 30. For Kingdom Publishers the streak counts months, so it is brightest at 12. If you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges, the lamp keeps a steady medium glow and no streak number shows anywhere.
faq_petRoom_q: How do I decorate my pet’s room?
faq_petRoom_a: Tap your pet's card on Home anywhere except on your pet (tapping your pet pats it), or long-press the card's name and choose Hat & Room…. Pick a tab (Hat, Window, Wall, Floor, Bed, Shelf, Light, or Sign) and tap a picture; the room at the top changes right away and the change is saved. Live window follows your clock and the season where you are (from your region; seasons are reversed south of the equator); turn it off to choose a time of day and a season, each of which can also stay Live. The sign on the wall can show your hours this month, your hours this service year, the months you shared in the ministry, your next plan, or this month's conversations and return visits, or nothing. Some items are open from the start. Each of the others opens up the first time your streak reaches the number on its flame: from 1 to 120 kept planned days for pioneers and other roles that log hours, or from 1 to 12 months in a row for publishers. Hats follow their own numbers (see the question about hats). Once an item opens up, it stays open, even if your streak ends later. If you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges, or you log hours but haven't made any plans, one more item opens up instead for each month you're active (any day with logged time, a visit, or a saved plan) since you adopted your pet, in a set order, and a locked item shows the month it opens up. Items that are already open stay open either way. Some items are secrets, which follow neither your streak nor the months; see the question about secret items.
faq_petHats_q: How do I get hats for my pet?
faq_petHats_a: Your pet can wear a hat, or none: 12 to start working toward, and secret hats you find along the way (see the question about secret items). Tap your pet's card on Home anywhere except on your pet, pick the Hat tab, and tap a hat; it's saved right away, and your pet wears it on Home, in its details, in shared pictures, and in the Home Screen widget (iPhone and iPad). The 12 open up with your streak like room items, on their own numbers: the first three come quickly, at 3, 5, and 9 kept planned days (or in your first month for publishers), and the rest take longer, up to 120 days (or 12 months). If you turned off Show streak, or you log hours but haven't made any plans, the first three open up in your first active month and the rest one month at a time. A locked hat shows the number or month it opens up at, and once a hat opens up it stays open. Your pet takes its hat off while it rolls over or lies down. Your buddies see your pet without its hat.
faq_petSecrets_q: What are the secret hats and room items?
faq_petSecrets_a: Besides the hats and room items that open up with your streak, every tab but Window and Sign has secret ones. Until you find one, it shows only as a dark shadow with a question mark and ??? for its name, and tapping it says only that it's a surprise. Each secret opens up on its own milestone as you keep going in the ministry and care for your pet; which one is part of the surprise. None depend on hours, none need a buddy, and none can be missed for good, so you can find any of them later. The first time you see one after it opens up, it says New; then pick it like any other item. Secrets you've found stay open, sync with your pet like other items, and come back from a backup. If a secret you expected hasn't shown up, open your pet's details again after your records sync; secrets are worked out on each device from what's stored there.
faq_petWidget_q: Can I see my pet on my home screen?
faq_petWidget_a: On iPhone and iPad, yes. Long-press your home screen, tap the + button, search for WitnessWork, and choose Pet Companion. Small shows your pet; medium adds its name, hearts, your streak, and what its wall sign shows; large shows its whole room with its name and hearts. The widget moves through the day on its own, and opening WitnessWork refreshes it. Until you adopt a pet, it asks you to choose one in the app. Android doesn’t have WitnessWork home screen widgets.
faq_petSync_q: Does my pet sync, and what do my buddies see?
faq_petSync_a: Your pet, its name, hat, room, the hats and room items it has opened up, and keepsakes sync between your devices with Device Sync, a Supporter feature, using the option you choose in Settings → Sync: Cloud Sync, which also syncs between iPhone and Android, or iCloud (Google Drive on Android). They're included in WitnessWork Backup (Settings → Account) and in backups from Settings → Backup & Restore too. Its hearts aren't stored: each device works them out from your records. With Buddies, your pet's kind, coat, and name are shared (not its hat) with your buddies, end-to-end encrypted. To stop sharing them, turn off Pet in Buddies Settings; the switch shows once you have a pet. Nothing else about your pet, and none of your records, is shared.
faq_petChange_q: Can I change or rename my pet?
faq_petChange_a: Yes. Tap your pet's card on Home (anywhere except on your pet) to open its details, then tap Rename or Change pet; or long-press the card's name for Rename… and Change Pet…. Rename lets you type a name of up to 20 characters; clear it and save to use the animal's name instead. Change pet picks another animal or coat for the same companion: it keeps its name, hearts, hat, room, and keepsakes. Names are yours and are never translated.
faq_petShare_q: How do I share a picture of my pet?
faq_petShare_a: Tap your pet's card on Home (anywhere except on your pet) and tap Share, or long-press the card's name and choose Share…. Its share card shows your pet in its room with its name and hearts, a few facts (your Service Streak once it reaches 3, unless you turned off Show streak in Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges; how many days you've been together; and how many hats it has opened up), and the WitnessWork name at the bottom. Tap Share to send the card as a picture with any app in the share sheet. Nothing is sent until you choose where it goes, and the picture holds nothing else about you or your records. If sharing fails, a message says so; try again, and if it keeps failing, close and reopen WitnessWork.

faq_syncRecovery_q: What happens to setup choices, deleted contacts, and reminders during sync?
faq_syncRecovery_a: Restart onboarding affects only this device. Choosing Set up fresh pauses iCloud sync until you explicitly enable it in Settings; then choose Merge both or Restore from iCloud as appropriate. Restore from iCloud reads other devices’ snapshots and replaces local data after confirmation. During onboarding, a device that already has records asks before replacing them, and Supporters can choose Merge instead. Keep this device’s data makes your other devices switch to this device’s data the next time they sync, replacing changes made on them before then. Restoring data does not send Buddies declines for plans absent from the backup. Recoverable deleted contact details are retained for up to 90 days, then removed while deletion evidence remains. Reminders are rebuilt on this device after merges and restores, keeping the reminder time chosen for each follow-up and plan; notification permission is required and only future reminders are scheduled. For recovery, keep the device with the latest records and export a backup before replacing data. Use private Help Center support if you need help.
faq_syncRemoveDevice_q: How do I remove an old device from sync?
faq_syncRemoveDevice_a: Each device that uses iCloud Sync keeps its own copy of your data in your iCloud, and that copy stays after you stop using the device, even after a reinstall or a new phone. Remove it when you no longer use a device, for example one you sold, replaced, or reset. On a device that still syncs, open Settings → iCloud Sync → Devices and tap Remove beside the old device. Devices not synced in 90 or more days are marked. Removing deletes only that device’s copy from iCloud, including details it still held of contacts deleted elsewhere. This device keeps everything it has already synced, and your other devices aren’t changed. If the removed device is still in use, it adds its data back the next time it syncs; turn off iCloud Sync on it first if you want it to stop. Before removing a device, this device must finish syncing its data; if asked, go back, tap Sync now, and fix any problem the status shows. If the device uses a newer version of WitnessWork, update this device first. Devices replaced by Rebuild iCloud data can be removed at any time. Photos aren’t stored per device, so removing a device doesn’t remove photos; use Remove iCloud photos for that. Devices is part of Settings → Sync on every option, all Supporter features: with iCloud the copies are in your iCloud, with Google Drive on Android in your Google Drive, and with Cloud Sync, removing a device deletes its copy from WitnessWork's server. If you need help, use the Help Center’s private support option and keep householder details out of public reports.

faq_badgesOverview_q: How do badges work, and where do I find them?
faq_badgesOverview_a: Badges celebrate steady habits in your ministry, like sharing each month, sending your report, and going back to see people. There's nothing to set up: WitnessWork checks your records and adds a badge when you reach one. To see yours, tap your profile picture, then Profile. Your badges sit right under your profile card; tap one to see it up close, or tap See all to open Badges, where you can see every badge you have and what helps each one grow next. Most badges grow through four levels: Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Pearl. A few one-time badges, like First Bible Study, stay hidden until you have them. When something you just did earns a badge, like logging time, checking off that you shared, saving a visit or plan, sending your report, answering Going, or confirming a buddy, it's celebrated right away. A badge that arrives another way, such as a plan's day arriving overnight, time logged on your watch or another device, or a buddy's reply, doesn't interrupt you: a New badge card at the top of Home names it instead. Tap View to see it up close, or the X to dismiss the card; either way the badge is saved and stays marked new on your profile until you open your badges. If one entry earns a badge and grows your streak to a milestone, the streak celebrates and the badge waits on Home. If your records already reach badges the first time WitnessWork checks them on a device, a one-time “Your badges are here” screen says how many you have: Take a look opens your profile, and Later closes it. It waits for a time you open WitnessWork without an update's tour. Badges reached by records you add or restore while setting up WitnessWork are added without it. Either way, your badges are already saved. Badges work on iOS and Android and update a moment after your records change and whenever you return to WitnessWork. They aren't the red number on the app icon, which counts unread items in the notification bell.
faq_badgesView_q: How do I see a badge up close or share it?
faq_badgesView_a: Tap any badge, on your profile, on the Badges screen, or on a buddy's page in Buddies, and it opens full screen: the badge, its level, what it counts, and when you earned it. “Found in your history” means older records reached it and the month isn't known. Under your own badges, a line like “Next: Pearl · 41 of 60 months” shows how far that badge is from its next level, or “All four levels collected” once you have Pearl; tap the info button beside it to see what helps it grow. A level you haven't reached yet shows “Not yet” and how to get there, and so does a level a buddy hasn't reached when you tap it under See all on their page. Tap the badge to spin it. To share one, take a screenshot: the screen shows your name, as in “Anna's badge,” and WitnessWork at the bottom, and nothing is sent anywhere on its own. Your name comes from your profile, in Settings → Profile; without a name, the screen leaves it off. Close the badge with the X, by swiping down, or with Back on Android. With Buddies, your buddies' reactions appear under your own badge, and a buddy's badge lets you send one; see the question about what buddies see.
faq_badgesMonths_q: Why do badges count months instead of hours?
faq_badgesMonths_a: So everyone grows at the same pace, whatever their circumstances. Every badge counts calendar months, never hours or goals. A month counts once, whether you shared for a few minutes or all day, and whether you mark that you shared or log hours as a pioneer. Badges never reset or depend on an unbroken run of months, so time off for illness, travel, or a hard season takes nothing away; the next month you share simply counts. Your streak is separate and never affects your badges. Year Round counts service years with at least 10 months of sharing, so two months off in a service year never count against you. Because each month counts only once, the highest level, Pearl, takes years. That's on purpose.
faq_badgesCollections_q: What does each badge count, and why didn't a month count?
faq_badgesCollections_a: Sharing the Good News counts months where you logged time or marked that you shared. Year Round counts service years with at least 10 of those months. Reports Sent counts months whose report you sent from WitnessWork or marked as already sent. Ready to Go counts months with a Plan, once the Plan's day arrives. Kind Words counts months with a visit where you talked with someone; Not at Home visits don't count. Return Visits counts months you went back to someone you had visited before. Next Time counts months with a Follow-up that has a topic. Keeping in Touch counts the most different months you've talked with one person, in person, by phone, or by letter. Two by Two counts months a buddy went with you on a Plan or Follow-up, and shows only where Buddies is available. If a month didn't count: hours carried over by the rollover option don't count on their own, visits that came with a contact someone shared with you are theirs and don't count, a Plan counts only once its day arrives, and Two by Two needs a buddy who answered Going. One-time badges mark a first: your first Bible study, and your first buddy.
faq_badgesBuddies_q: What do my buddies see, how do reactions work, and how do I stop sharing badges or badge alerts?
faq_badgesBuddies_a: Your buddies see the badges you have, each at its highest level, in a row on your page in Buddies. See all there shows each collection with the levels you've reached and the ones still ahead, plus your one-time badges. They never see your progress, counts, or dates. In data protection mode, First Bible Study isn't shared. To stop sharing badges, turn off Badges in Buddies Settings. When a buddy gets a new badge, you get an alert with their name and the badge, like “Levi earned a badge” with “Year Round, Silver” below it; tap it to open their page. You get at most one alert per buddy a day, and later badges that day arrive quietly in the notification bell. Badges found in imported or restored history, and one-time badges, aren't announced. To encourage a buddy, open their page in Buddies, tap one of their badges, and pick a reaction: 🎉, 🎊, 🔥, 👏, 👍, or 🙌. You can react to each badge once; picking another reaction replaces the first. Only that buddy sees who reacted, and nothing else is sent: no message, and none of your own badges. If you're offline, your reaction is sent when you're back online. When a buddy reacts to one of your badges, you get an alert like “Anna reacted 🔥 to your badge,” at most once per buddy a day, and the reaction appears in the notification bell and when you open that badge. To stop alerts for new badges and reactions on a device, turn off Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings; both still appear in the notification bell. With Show badges off, you can't react, and reactions to your badges aren't shown.
faq_badgesBuddyNews_q: Where do my buddies' new badges and reactions show up?
faq_badgesBuddyNews_a: In the notification bell on Home, under From your buddies, below anything waiting for your answer. A buddy's new badge shows the badge with six reactions: 🎉, 🎊, 🔥, 👏, 👍, and 🙌. Tap one to encourage them right away. After that, the row shows what you sent; tap Change to pick another. Tap the row or its badge to see the badge full screen, marked New if you hadn't seen it yet. Several badges from one buddy within a day share one row. When a buddy reacts to one of your badges, tap it to open your badge with every buddy's reaction. Buddies' news never adds to the red number on the bell or the app icon; a small dot on the bell means something new from your buddies. It says only Today, This week, or Earlier, never the time. Dismiss it with X or Clear All, or let it clear on its own after 30 days. It shows only for your current buddies, wherever Buddies is available, on iPhone, iPad, and Android, and only while Show badges is on. To stop the alerts but keep the news in the bell, turn off Badge Alerts in Buddies Settings. If you're offline, your reaction is saved and sent when you're back online. When you get a new badge yourself and share badges with your buddies, the New badge card says who will see it, like “Ben and Grace will see it.” To stop sharing badges, turn off Badges in Buddies Settings.
faq_badgesKeep_q: Can I lose my badges, move them to a new device, or hide them?
faq_badgesKeep_a: Badges are keepsakes: once you have one, it stays, even if you later delete the time, visits, or plans behind it, or a buddy leaves. Progress toward the next level is kept too when data protection mode suggests deleting old details. Your badges sync between your devices when sync is on and are included in backup files, so restoring a backup on a new phone brings them back. When imported or restored history reaches new badges, they're added quietly with one summary instead of a celebration for each, or with no summary at all when you import or restore while setting up WitnessWork. To hide badges, open Settings → Preferences → Streaks & Badges and turn off Show badges. That hides them everywhere, including from your buddies and celebrations, without forgetting them; turn it back on and they return.

faq_accountOverview_a: Your WitnessWork account is anonymous: there's no email, phone number, or password. Your phone makes a secret account key the first time you use Buddies, Notes Import, or Backup, or view your recovery key, and WitnessWork's server knows you only by a random account number. Find it in Settings → Account. Each device proves it's the genuine WitnessWork app when it connects to your account (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). The key stays on your devices: in iCloud Keychain on iPhone and iPad, and in Google's Block Store backup on Android. Buddies uses it for your identity, and the server never sees your name or anything you share with buddies. Your service records, contacts, and notes stay on your device; if you turn on Backup in Settings → Account, the server also keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy that only your devices can read.
faq_accountRecoveryKey_q: What is my recovery key, and how do I keep it safe?
faq_accountRecoveryKey_a: Your recovery key is your account key written out as WW1- and eleven groups of five letters and numbers. To see it, go to Settings → Account → Show Recovery Key; your phone asks for Face ID, Touch ID, your passcode, or your screen lock first when one is set. Copy it into a password manager, or share it to a private note or print it, and keep it somewhere only you can reach. Anyone who has it has your account, including your Buddies, so don't send it to other people or post it. If you lose it, view it again on any phone that still uses your account. If you think someone else has it, delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data): that removes your buddies and gives you a new account and recovery key. If you lose every phone and the key, no one can recover the account, including us.
faq_accountRecoveryKeyUse_q: How do I use my recovery key on a new phone?
faq_accountRecoveryKeyUse_a: If you still have your old phone, Set Up Another Device is easier: see "How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?". Otherwise, install WitnessWork on the new phone, go to Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key, and enter your key. It works between iPhone and Android. Case, spaces, and dashes don't matter, and the app tells you when a character is mistyped. If that phone already used Buddies with a different account, the app asks you first, and its Buddies data is deleted from the phone. While other devices are still signed in to that account, its buddies stay on them; on the account's last device, its buddies are removed for good. On iPhone and iPad, the key also replaces the account on your other Apple devices that use the same iCloud Keychain. The recovery key brings your account and Buddies identity. If your account has a backup (Settings → Account → Backup), the app then offers to restore your service records, contacts, and notes; otherwise Cloud Sync brings them over once it's on for the new phone (Settings → Sync), or you can move them with iCloud Sync, Google Drive Sync, or Settings → Backup & Restore.
faq_accountActivity_q: How do I see which devices use my account?
faq_accountActivity_a: Go to Settings → Account → Signed-In Devices. It lists every device signed in to your WitnessWork account and when each was last active, with "This device" marked. Tap another device to sign it out, for example a phone you sold or lost. Signing out ends that device's connection, but if WitnessWork on it still has your account, it signs back in the next time it's used. If you think someone else has your account, delete your Buddies data (Buddies Settings → Delete My Buddies Data) to get a new account and recovery key, then set up your other devices again. Settings → Account → Account Activity shows your account's history for the last 400 days: sign-ins and sign-outs, devices signed out from another device, your account sent to a new phone, backups deleted or downloaded, Buddies set up or its data deleted, and suspensions. "Signed out … to protect your account" means a device's sign-in was used again after it had been replaced, which can mean someone copied it; check Signed-In Devices for anything you don't recognize. Device names are encrypted so only your devices can read them, and WitnessWork's server doesn't keep locations, IP addresses, or anything you share. Both need the internet, and they appear once your account is set up.
faq_accountHandoff_q: How do I move to a new phone or switch between iPhone and Android?
faq_accountHandoff_a: Use Set Up Another Device. It works between any two phones, including from iPhone to Android and back. On your old phone, go to Settings → Account → Set Up Another Device to show a QR code. On the new phone, install WitnessWork and choose Sign In with QR Code: during setup, tap "I already use WitnessWork", then From your other phone; after setup, it's in Settings → Account. Both phones show the same six-digit code. Check that they match, then tap Allow on the old phone. Both phones need the internet, and a code expires after 10 minutes. Your account and your buddies move to the new phone, and your old phone stays signed in. If the new phone used Buddies with another account, it asks first: that account's buddies stay on its other signed-in devices, or are removed for good if this was its last one. To bring your service records, contacts, and notes too, use Cloud Sync, which works between iPhone and Android: once it's on for the new phone, your records arrive without a restore step. Or turn on Backup in Settings → Account on the old phone first: the new phone then offers to restore them. iCloud Sync and Google Drive Sync work between phones of the same kind, and a backup file from Settings → Backup & Restore works between any two. The account travels end-to-end encrypted, so the server can't read it, and it keeps nothing once the new phone has it.
faq_accountHandoffTrouble_q: What if signing in with a QR code doesn't work?
faq_accountHandoffTrouble_a: Make a new code on your old phone (Make a New Code) and scan it again. Each code works once and only for 10 minutes. Check that both phones are connected to the internet. Both phones need WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play: a device that can't be verified can't use your account (see "Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?"). If the codes on the two phones don't match, tap Don't Allow and start over, since another phone may have scanned your code. If the new phone can't scan, check that WitnessWork may use its camera in your phone's settings. If you no longer have your old phone, use your recovery key instead: on the new phone, go to Settings → Account → Use a Recovery Key. If it still doesn't work, contact support from the Help Center; never send your recovery key.
faq_accountVerification_q: Why does WitnessWork say it can't verify this device?
faq_accountVerification_a: Your account, Buddies, Backup, Set Up Another Device, and Notes Import work only in the genuine WitnessWork app. When a device first connects to your account, and again about every 90 days, WitnessWork asks Apple (App Attest, on iPhone and iPad) or Google (Play Integrity, on Android) to confirm the app and device are genuine. Apple and Google receive only that check, never your records, your account number, or your account key. Simulators, emulators, rooted devices, custom system software, and modified or unofficial copies of the app can't be verified; on Android the device also needs the Google Play Store and Google Play services, up to date. If Settings → Account says Not verified yet, Apple or Google couldn't be reached just then: wait a few minutes and tap Try Again. If it says Can't verify this device, reinstall WitnessWork from the App Store or Google Play and update the device's system software, then tap Try Again. Everything else in WitnessWork works on that device as usual, and your data stays on it. If a genuine device still can't be verified, contact support from the Help Center.
faq_updateRequired_q: Why does WitnessWork say Update Required?
faq_updateRequired_a: Sometimes WitnessWork's server changes in a way older versions of the app can't follow. When your version is too old to work with it, WitnessWork shows Update Required and waits until you update. Tap Update WitnessWork to open the App Store or Google Play, install the update, then open WitnessWork again. Your service records, contacts, and notes stay on your device and are all there after the update. If the store doesn't show an update, close the store app, open it again, and check for updates there.
backup_sectionInfo: WitnessWork keeps an end-to-end encrypted copy of your service records, contacts, notes, plans, and settings. Only your devices can read it, not WitnessWork. It's free. Photos aren't included. On a new phone, you can restore it after Set Up Another Device or with your recovery key.

cloudSyncOffer_body: Cloud Sync is always end-to-end encrypted, so only your devices can read your data, and it works across iPhone and Android. WitnessWork doesn't encrypt iCloud sync end to end. Your data on this device is kept and combined with your other devices on Cloud Sync.
cloudSyncOffer_bodyAndroid: Cloud Sync is always end-to-end encrypted, so only your devices can read your data, and it works across Android and iPhone. WitnessWork doesn't encrypt Google Drive sync end to end. Your data on this device is kept and combined with your other devices on Cloud Sync.
syncOption_info: Each device syncs one way at a time, and only with devices that sync the same way. Cloud Sync stores an end-to-end encrypted copy of each device's data on WitnessWork's server: only your devices have the key, and it works on iPhone and Android. iCloud stores a copy in your iCloud Drive; Apple encrypts it, but WitnessWork doesn't encrypt it end to end, and it works only on Apple devices.

Google Drive stores a copy in a hidden folder of your Google Drive; Google protects it, but WitnessWork doesn't encrypt it end to end, and it works only on Android.
